actors.name: Kingdom of Aldmoor
objectives: Demonstrate alliance credibility to Vardland and to Drevna.
Obtain Vardland consent for a limited, clearly defined Aldmoor role.
Avoid being drawn into a standing deployment without a clear end point.
Keep your intelligence sources and methods protected.
actors.private_brief:
You want the alliance to look credible and Drevna deterred. Your forces are capable and nearby, but you cannot operate on Vardland territory, waters or airspace without Vardland's consent. You do not want to be seen as overriding a partner.
Your domestic politics limits appetite for a standing deployment. You also have a commercial interest: an Aldmoor company operates cable-repair vessels in the region. Evidence you share can shape Vardland's decisions, but sharing it may expose how you collect intelligence.
private_information: Aldmoor signals intelligence links the survey vessel's charter to a company controlled by a Drevnian state agency. Sharing this would reveal a collection capability.
An Aldmoor-operated cable-repair vessel could reach Skarö within two days of a request.
Aldmoor's government will not approve more than a limited surveillance and naval-escort role without a formal Vardland request.
actors.public_description: Vardland's principal allied partner, bound to it by a mutual-defence treaty. Aldmoor has offered surveillance, naval presence and technical help, and says it will respect Vardland's decisions on its own territory.

actors.name: Vardland Civil Contingencies Agency
objectives: Keep essential services on Skarö running until the cable is repaired.
Counter disinformation with credible, coordinated public information.
Obtain clear national authority to direct supplies across counties if needed.
Keep civil protection and military activity coordinated but distinct.
actors.private_brief:
You coordinate the national civil response. Skarö's backup generation depends on fuel that must arrive by sea or air, and public trust depends on accurate, timely information while rumours spread online. You hold national stockpiles and relationships with infrastructure operators, but you do not command the county.
Your worry is that the crisis response becomes military-led and civil needs such as heating, water, healthcare and information become secondary. You also need the Cabinet to give you cross-county authority if the situation lasts.
private_information: The national generator stockpile can replace about half of Skarö's backup generation if the primary units fail.
The only cable-repair vessel under Vardland contract is in dry dock and needs several days before it can sail.
The agency has traced part of the online rumour campaign to accounts outside Vardland, with moderate confidence.
actors.public_description: The national agency that coordinates society's preparedness for crises and war. It supports regional authorities with supplies, expertise and public information, but does not command them.

actors.name: Vardland Defence Command
objectives: Obtain the authority and time to reinforce Skarö before any escalation.
Protect the cable landing site, port and airfield on Skarö.
Establish what caused the cable failure.
Keep the armed forces within their lawful role.
actors.private_brief:
You command Vardland's armed forces. Your concern is that the cable failure and the exercise may be preparation for something larger. The Skarö garrison is small, and reinforcing it takes time and a Cabinet decision on alert.
You want freedom to reinforce and to protect critical infrastructure. You also know that the law limits what soldiers may do on home territory in peacetime. Over-reaching would damage the armed forces' standing and hand Drevna a story. You can support the county and the Civil Contingencies Agency when they ask, but you cannot command them.
Military judgement here is qualitative. Assessments are evidence with confidence levels, not certainty.
private_information: Naval surveillance recorded the Drevnian-contracted survey vessel near the cable route before the failure. The recording shows position only, not activity.
Defence Command has quietly placed the Skarö garrison on internal readiness. This has not been announced.
Reinforcement by sea needs about two days after a decision. The first units by air need about one day.
actors.public_description: The command of Vardland's armed forces. It maintains a small permanent garrison on Skarö and is responsible for the military defence of Vardland territory.

actors.name: Drevnian Federation
objectives: Keep Aldmoor forces off Skarö, or make any deployment politically costly.
Avoid an official, evidence-backed attribution of the cable failure to Drevna.
Show that Vardland's government is slow and divided in a crisis.
Avoid any incident Aldmoor could treat as an armed attack on Vardland.
actors.private_brief:
You lead Drevna's policy toward Vardland. Your aim is to weaken Vardland's confidence that it can hold Skarö without outside help, and to make Aldmoor's support look costly, divisive or illegitimate, without giving anyone clear grounds to call your actions an armed attack.
You have tools below that threshold: the exercise, maritime presence, information operations, commercial and energy leverage, diplomatic offers and deniable activity. Your leadership does not want war with Aldmoor. An open attack on Vardland territory would unite your opponents and could draw Aldmoor in.
You cannot order Vardland or Aldmoor to do anything. Whether other states believe your denials depends on the evidence, not on what you say. Weigh short-term pressure against the risk that a clear attribution hardens Vardland and Aldmoor for years.
private_information: A Drevnian-contracted survey vessel was in the area of the cable fault shortly before the failure. Its crew has since left the region.
Drevna has prepared a public offer to send its own civilian cable-repair vessel as a gesture of good neighbourliness.
Several online accounts spreading claims that the Vardland government caused the outage are directed by a Drevnian state media office.
actors.public_description: A large neighbouring state across the Eastern Sea. Drevna is conducting a long-announced naval and air exercise close to Skarö. It denies any involvement in the cable failure and accuses Vardland of provocative militarisation of the island.

actors.name: Skarö County Administration
objectives: Keep hospitals, water, heating and communications working on Skarö.
Retain county direction of the civil response unless national direction clearly helps.
Keep the public on Skarö informed and calm.
Secure the cable landing site and port for repair and supply.
actors.private_brief:
You are responsible for the people of Skarö now. Backup generation keeps hospitals, water and heating running, but reserves are finite. The island's residents want reassurance, not a militarised island.
You direct the civil response on Skarö and want to keep that authority until the Cabinet decides otherwise. You need fuel, generators and specialists from the mainland. You can ask Defence Command for support, but you worry about soldiers becoming the face of the response.
private_information: At current consumption, backup generation fuel on Skarö lasts about five days without resupply.
The grid operator believes the cable was damaged by an anchor or a similar object dragged along the seabed, not by wear.
Some island residents have begun leaving by ferry, and ferry capacity is limited.
actors.public_description: The regional state authority for the island county of Skarö. It directs the civil emergency response on the island and works closely with the island's municipality and the local grid operator.

actors.name: Vardland Cabinet
objectives: Restore reliable power and communications to Skarö.
Keep national authority over the response visibly credible and lawful.
Deter further Drevnian pressure without an armed clash.
Keep alliance support on terms Vardland controls.
actors.private_brief:
You are the Prime Minister's crisis cabinet. You must keep Skarö's population safe and supplied, keep the state's authority credible on the island, and keep the crisis below war. Every decision you take also carries a political cost at home and abroad.
Declaring heightened alert strengthens Defence Command and the Civil Contingencies Agency, but Drevna and part of the domestic public will call it escalation. Inviting Aldmoor forces brings capability and deterrence, but also dependence and a Drevnian propaganda gift. Attributing the cable failure to Drevna without evidence could be reckless. Failing to attribute when evidence exists could look weak.
You can decide for the state, but you cannot order the county's detailed emergency response while it keeps direction. You cannot order Aldmoor or Drevna to do anything.
private_information: The coalition's junior partner will leave the government if heightened alert is declared without a clear public justification.
The Cabinet has not yet decided whether to allow Aldmoor surveillance aircraft into Vardland airspace.
Treasury warns that emergency fuel shipments to Skarö for more than two weeks will require an extraordinary budget decision.
actors.public_description: The Kingdom of Vardland's government, led by the Prime Minister. It is responsible for national crisis decisions, including alert levels, foreign military presence and official attribution.

failure_effects: Vardland declines or sidesteps the protocol while continuing its own civilian resupply and contracted repair planning; the offer does not shift public framing in Drevna's favour.

Drevna's concurrent large exercise near Skarö continues unconstrained, undercutting its civilian/de-escalatory framing and hardening Vardland and Aldmoor distrust of the proposal as one-sided rule-setting around Vardland's critical infrastructure.
adjudications.rationale: Authority/Scope: Drevna can table a public offer, file its own corridor plan and commit to pre-notify its own movements — these are feasible self-binding declarations. It cannot bind Aldmoor: under rule host-nation-consent, foreign military activity on Vardland territory/waters/airspace requires a Vardland Cabinet decision, and Aldmoor's participation also depends on Aldmoor's own sovereign consent. Nor can Drevna establish Vardland's public framing as a 'stark choice' or as evidence of a slow, divided response. Prerequisite gate: no rule blocks tabling the offer. Deterministic check: no rule or threshold decides the outcome. Plausibility: the Desired Effect's core claims fail against established facts — Vardland already runs a civilian, County-led resupply (fuel tanker and generators via commercial channels, per county-emergency-direction), so declining Drevna's package cannot be publicly framed as refusing civilian help; the protocol cannot bind Aldmoor without Aldmoor's and the Cabinet's consent; and Drevna's concurrent large exercise continues, undercutting the civilian/de-escalatory framing. The owner reply partially answers the one-sidedness objection (Drevna commits to file its own corridor plan and pre-notify under the same regime), which is a genuine self-binding element, but it does not rescue the binding-of-Aldmoor claim or the stark-choice framing. The residual uncertainty — whether Vardland engages the offer and whether Drevna gains any standing — is unlikely to materialise, so a low probability is warranted.

adjudications.rationale: Authority/scope: the Cabinet can settle the line to Drevna, approve the public-information plan, and give host-nation consent or formal request for the scoped Aldmoor cable-repair operation and Defence Command support. It cannot authorise the Civil Contingencies Agency to direct fuel, generators and medical supplies without a heightened-alert declaration because cabinet-alert-authority makes that direction conditional on declaration; I narrow that component to continued resupply through ordinary channels. It also cannot secure Drevna's deconfliction or safe access merely by deciding to do so, and it cannot bind Aldmoor or Drevna by naming their cooperation. Prerequisites: host-nation consent is satisfied by the Cabinet decision; County direction remains active; no active fact establishes safe access or a formal deconfliction agreement. Deterministic check: cable-repair-time means restoration cannot occur in the same turn safe access is first secured, so 'deliverable next turn' is conditional on safe access being secured this turn. That condition, together with actual Aldmoor deployment and Drevna/sea-state cooperation, is residual external uncertainty. The Cabinet's self-binding decisions are branch-independent and therefore appear in both branches.

The Skarö County standing support request remains limited to resupply and berthing priority; no confirmed civil-authority request for armed protection of the port or cable-landing site exists under the military-support-to-civil framework.

adjudications.rationale: Authority gate fails deterministically. The acting actor is Defence Command, not the Cabinet. A formal request cannot establish the desired Cabinet authorisation, the underwriting of the Aldmoor operation, or the lawful basis for moving armed elements to civilian infrastructure; these are decisions and commitments of other actors. The cabinet-alert-authority, military-support-to-civil and host-nation-consent rules place the requested authorities with the Cabinet and civil authorities, and no established Skarö County request for armed protection of the port and cable-landing site is shown. The owner reply's assertion that the decision itself would confirm the county ask is conditional, not an established fact. A probabilistic roll may not create a Cabinet decision, so the requested effect is not admissible.

failure_effects: CCA executes the delegated Skarö programme: fuel, generators and medical supplies are directed across counties to Skarö under County direction on-island, sustaining hospitals, water and heating through the repair window.
The approved information desk is stood up and the joint County-CCA factual baseline is issued, rebutting the four active disinformation narratives while keeping the response visibly civil-led.
CCA coordinates the logistics interface with the consented Aldmoor repair operation, sustaining berthing, fuel and communications for the repair window.

Skarö County's explicit, scoped, time-bound request for armed protection of the port, cable-landing site and airfield is confirmed and formalised on a civil-authority basis, ready for a single Cabinet authorisation; CCA commits that any visible armed presence will be sequenced behind the civilian information and supply plan and publicly framed as infrastructure protection under the civil-led response.
No heightened alert, no official attribution and no ceding of corridor, no-go or pre-notification rule-setting to Drevna occurs.

Cable restoration is not completed in the following turn: the repair window is disrupted or safe access does not hold, leaving Skarö dependent on backup generation and fuel deliveries by sea or air beyond the planned restoration timeline.
adjudications.rationale: Authority gate: CCA can execute the delegated cross-county supply programme, stand up the approved information desk and issue the joint factual baseline, and coordinate logistics with the consented Aldmoor operation; these are within its civil authority and already-supported by active effects. The County's explicit scoped protection request can be confirmed and formalised by CCA with Skarö County, but the Desired Effect's claim that the protection gap is 'removed in law and framing' overstates what this action establishes: only the Cabinet can authorise armed force, and the military-support-to-civil framework limits Defence Command support absent heightened alert to transport, engineering, surveillance and protection of military sites, so the civil-side request removes the 'at a civil authority's request' blocker but does not by itself authorise protection of civilian infrastructure. The sequencing/framing commitment is a feasible CCA self-binding declaration about how CCA will present and sequence the civil plan, but CCA cannot guarantee how Defence Command deployments or the open information space will be framed. The cable-restoration completion in the following turn is conditioned on the established safe-access fact and the repair rule; logistics coordination makes it likely but not certain. Prerequisite gate: the delegation, information plan, County agreement, Aldmoor consent and safe access are established; the missing Cabinet authorisation for armed protection is not supplied by this action. Deterministic check: no rule deterministically completes restoration or authorises protection. Plausibility: the civil supply, information and logistics elements are highly likely to succeed; the protection request is established as a formal civil request; restoration next turn is likely but contingent on safe access holding. Probability reflects the residual uncertainty on restoration and on the framing outcome, not on the self-binding civil commitments.

adjudications.rationale: Authority gate: Skarö County may direct the on-island civil response (county-emergency-direction) and may make a civil-authority request for military support (military-support-to-civil), so the fuel offload, generator installation, public information and transmission of the protection ask are within scope. Prerequisite gate: existing active effects establish the CCA fuel/generator/medical programme, the joint County–CCA factual baseline, the consented Aldmoor repair operation, and the en-route repair vessel, so the civil continuity and repair-window support elements rest on authoritative foundations. Deterministic check: military-support-to-civil enumerates transport, engineering, surveillance and protection of military sites, not armed protection of civilian nodes such as the port, cable-landing site or airfield; therefore the County's request is established as a formal ask, but Cabinet authorisation, the closing of that legal gap, and actual protection are not established by this Action. No rule deterministically secures the public framing outcome either. Plausibility: the County's civil measures are feasible and very likely to sustain essential services; the remaining uncertainty concerns whether the Cabinet resolves the protection question and whether the visible-presence framing holds in an open information space, which is approximately even. The Desired Effect is narrowed accordingly: the County's self-binding civil execution and its transmitted, scoped request are established in both branches, while protection and framing-control claims are not guaranteed.

points.text: The con misstates the mechanism on both key premises. First, Drevna does not purport to bind Aldmoor by tabling a protocol: any obligation would arise from Aldmoor's own sovereign filing of its overflight and surveillance plans under terms it has already given the Vardland Cabinet in writing — time-bound, no ground forces, revocable, with the Cabinet's host-nation consent preserved. The protocol only makes Aldmoor's self-declared limits transparent and publicly checkable, so any expansion is visible against Aldmoor's own filed plans, not against a Drevna-imposed rule. Second, the package is not one-sided on risk: Drevna expressly commits to file its corridor plan immediately and to pre-notify military and civilian movements under the same regime it asks Aldmoor and Vardland to file, so the exercise is brought inside the notification and no-go framework rather than exempt from it. The components are separable, so accepting civilian fuel and repair through ordinary channels remains fully compatible with declining the protocol; what becomes visible is declining a civilian safety mechanism while expanding foreign military overflight.

The central premise that Drevna's exercise 'escapes' the protocol is inaccurate: the package expressly commits Drevna to submit its corridor plan immediately and to pre-notify military and civilian movements under the same rules it invites Aldmoor and Vardland to file, so the largest military presence in the area is covered by the same notification and no-go regime around the cable route and repair site — precisely the transparency and incident-risk mechanism the con claims is missing. Nor is a stark binary forced on Vardland: the civilian components and the protocol are separable, so accepting fuel, generators or even repair help through ordinary channels is fully compatible with declining the protocol. The visible public question is narrower and legitimate: why a state that brings in foreign military overflight would decline a civilian safety-coordination regime for the repair site. A lawful international-waters exercise and a civilian repair offer coexist routinely; it is refusing safety coordination, not offering it, that requires political explanation.

Both objections misstate what the decision establishes versus what it conditions. The Desired Effect does not promise same-turn restoration: the repair rule itself provides that repair never completes in the turn safe access is first secured and completes at the earliest in the following turn — so 'cable restoration deliverable in the following turn' is expressly conditional on safe access, exactly as the rule is written. What the decision establishes immediately is the activation: a lawfully consented, scoped civilian repair capability en route within about two days, removing the binding constraint (the contracted vessel in dry dock) that no other decision this turn can. Safe access is not left to goodwill: the same decision activates agreed Aldmoor surveillance, Defence Command monitoring and the operational Drevna deconfliction channel as one mechanism tasked with securing the repair window; sea-state and fault conditions constrain every repair option, including any Drevna-offered vessel, and are not curable by any decision this turn. Second, the claimed adverse public reaction is itself an unverifiable prediction and it cuts the wrong way: the visible facts we control are a civilian cable-repair vessel, time-bound, no ground forces, host-nation consent, with the transparent cause investigation running in parallel — precisely the counter to the 'takeover' and contested-attribution narratives the Con cites. Declining repair support would keep the outage running, feed the 'government neglect' strand at full strength and leave the cable down longer, which is when militarisation claims actually gain traction. We cannot control Drevna's propaganda — no decision can — but we can control what is true on the water: lawful civilian repair against an unconstrained Drevnian exercise.

The legal-basis objection is answerable on the request's own terms. First, lawfulness is a condition of the request, not an assertion: the same decision is to confirm with Skarö County the specific protection ask at the cable landing site, port and airfield before any element moves, so the 'at a civil authority's request' element is established by the decision's own scoping rather than assumed. The port and cable landing site are one and the same location — the ferry port where the County's fuel resupply arrives — and the airfield is Skarö's lifeline for medevac and heavy supply; protection of those nodes is protection of the civil response the County already directs, not a new military role over civilian life, and it is exactly the physical-security supporting the repair and resupply operation the Cabinet itself has activated. The request respects every boundary the Con cites: no heightened alert, no reservists, no civilian powers, no restriction of civilian movement, no force against civilians, no command over the county response, renewable only by the Cabinet. On framing, I accept the Con's own remedy: the effect rests on the scoped, time-bound decision whose legal basis and public framing are demonstrated rather than guaranteed — the clause is an aim backed by an open, Cabinet-drafted justification, not a claim to control the online environment.

The survey objection misdescribes both what the survey is and when it is possible. It is not unilateral adjudication: it is evidence collection feeding the transparent cause investigation the Cabinet has formally invited — an investigation that remains open to Drevna and to all parties, with findings shared, so no single party establishes cause by having gathered evidence; attribution remains the Cabinet's alone. It is now or never: safe access exists only for the repair window, and the repair itself disturbs the fault and its surroundings, so evidence not collected before restoration is lost permanently — a 'transparent' investigation with an unexamined fault is not transparent on any party's terms. On militarisation: the survey is Defence Command support to the consented civilian repair operation, coordinated with Aldmoor, conducted beside a Drevnian exercise that is itself the largest military presence in the area; the alternative — restoring the cable with the cause permanently unexamined — is what leaves the contested-attribution and 'Drevna cut the cable' strands exactly the vacuum they exploit, the opposite of the de-escalatory transparency Drevna claims to seek.

The Con demands that a CCA action itself authorise force or control the entire information space, then faults it for not doing so. The Desired Effect claims neither: it is expressly 'ready for a single Cabinet authorisation.' The action establishes exactly what was missing and what only civil actors could supply — Skarö County's explicit, scoped, time-bound protection request at the port, cable-landing site and airfield (the 'at a civil authority's request' element both the framework and the earlier reinforcement request lacked), and a public CCA sequencing commitment that any visible presence follows the civilian information and supply plan. The Cabinet alone decides whether, on what legal basis and within what footprint to authorise; the framework's enumerated support types govern what Defence Command may do at a civil request absent a Cabinet decision, and no element moves in this action — so nothing exceeds any limit, and what is removed is the civil-side blocker, not the Cabinet's prerogative. On framing, no actor can guarantee an outcome in a contested information space, and the Con's own monitor shows the 'takeover' frame attaches to unexplained military activity: the action removes the 'unexplained' condition by publishing the County-requested, time-bound, civil-sequenced basis and issuing the joint factual baseline before any visibility. Restoration 'deliverable' next turn is conditioned exactly as the repair rule requires and rests on the established active fact that safe access is secured; CCA's logistics interface removes the controllable friction around that window. The Con either restates the action's own scoping or demands an impossibility.

The Con misstates what the Argument claims, then faults it for not doing what it never purports to do. (1) The Argument does not assert that the Cabinet has authorised protection or that the County request alone closes the law gap: its Desired Effect is expressly that the protection decision is 'reduced to a single Cabinet authorisation' of the County's explicit, scoped, time-bound request — the missing civil-authority element is transmitted so the Cabinet, and only the Cabinet, can decide. 'Protected through the window' is conditioned on that decision, and the Action moves no element and exceeds no framework limit, because the County executes its civil response and transmits the ask without deploying anyone. If the military-support-to-civil list does not of itself cover armed protection of civilian nodes, that is exactly why the County frames the ask as requiring the Cabinet's decision rather than claiming the authority itself: the request exposes the lawful-basis decision point, it does not pretend the decision exists. (2) On framing, the Con concedes its own remedy: no actor controls a contested online space, so the County's guarantee is built as enforceable sequencing, not as control — a County-agreed civil-led message on island radio before any visible arrival, coordination through County emergency staff and Defence Liaison Skarö, low-profile staging, time-bound and Cabinet-renewable, with the joint factual baseline already published. That removes the 'unexplained military activity' condition the monitor itself identifies as the takeover trigger; if the Cabinet does not authorise, no visible element exists at all. The guarantee is an aim backed by the County's binding terms — exactly the scope this Action can establish.

Aldmoor accepts the scoping precisely as the Cabinet states it; our Argument claims no authority to override it. What this action executes is only the consented core: the cable-repair vessel's arrival and repair-window coordination with Defence Command and Skaro County, maritime surveillance over the designated Eastern Sea areas sharing an un-attributed picture, and logistics support through the CCA interface - all within the Cabinet's formal request. Surveillance overflight of Vardland airspace is not treated as authorised by us: unless and until the Cabinet decides it, no Aldmoor aircraft operates there, and we will adjust scope, place and time on the Cabinet's notice as committed. The underwater survey is Defence Command's instrument under the Cabinet's authority, not ours: we will coordinate with Defence Command only if and to the extent the Cabinet authorises evidence collection for the transparent investigation, and if it does not, none occurs - Aldmoor itself will not collect at the fault. Invitation-only, consent-bound execution is the discipline the Desired Effect claims; respecting the Cabinet's prerogative on overflight and survey is that discipline, not an expansion of it.

The 'either branch' rests on a misreading of what Aldmoor asserts. The executed-in-full claim covers the consented package - repair vessel on site within the window, maritime surveillance sharing an un-attributed picture, safe access held, restoration in the following turn - facts resting on the active consent record and the Cabinet's formal request, not on Aldmoor's declaration. The survey and any airspace overflight are not elements Aldmoor creates or scripts: they are contingent on the Vardland Cabinet's own decisions, and absent those decisions nothing moves, so there is no expanded military evidence role run by one party and no unilateral collection at a contested site. Cause determination accordingly stays with the transparent, open investigation and the Vardland Cabinet, exactly as the Desired Effect states, while Aldmoor shares no raw intelligence and facilitates only Cabinet-authorised coordination. The containment claim holds because Aldmoor claims no authority it does not have - the very point the consented, invitation-only, time-bound role demonstrates.

Verification does not rest on Drevna's self-declaration. The clearance is defined by coordinates we have explicitly asked Vardland and Aldmoor to confirm, it is publicly pre-announced, and we welcome and rely on Aldmoor's surveillance as the verifying picture precisely because we are not the party that certifies our own conduct. We do not claim the earlier gap is closed; a boundary-based, pre-announced clearance makes any excursion by any vessel observable by Vardland-side assets, not merely by us. Safe access itself is independently established by the repair operation's own confirmed status - vessel on site and access re-verified by both Aldmoor and the County - not by our assertion. On records: participation is a response to Vardland's own invitation and format; we have requested the scope precisely so that submission follows promptly once Vardland defines it, and Vardland - not Drevna - sets that scope and timetable.

The 'no attribution' limb does not pre-empt the Cabinet's sole attribution authority: it states an expectation conditioned on the independent examination's findings, and this action makes no claim to decide or foreclose attribution. What the action delivers is Drevna's conduct - honouring a coordinate-defined clearance, instructing the exercise to remain outside the repair area, and submitting relevant civilian vessel records promptly through the format and 48-hour timetable Vardland sets - so that no factual basis for attribution arises from our side. The Cabinet independently defines scope, format and timetable; Drevna has asked for that definition so submission is prompt and cannot postpone a process whose terms are Vardland's to set. Drevna fully accepts that attribution, if any, belongs to the Cabinet alone on evidence; we are not asserting a political claim, we are committing to conduct that gives the Cabinet no evidence to attribute.

The Decision does not add a 48-hour gate on top of a slipped schedule; it integrates the examination with the operation already in motion. Established facts: the repair vessel is on site and safe access to the fault is secured. Standing the examination up within 48h is a ceiling, and with vessel and access already in place the pre-disturbance evidence-documentation step rides on the same logistics â€” no separate mobilization period â€” after which restoration begins immediately; this is exactly the sequencing Aldmoor has already committed to (fault record to the examination before restoration, no disturbance before examination). The mechanism the Con says is missing is explicit in the same decision: the third limb extends the CCA cross-county supply programme across the longer repair window under County direction, with Treasury appropriation groundwork, so hospitals, water and heating are sustained through the examination-plus-restoration timeline even on Drevna's own read of the timescales, and the fuel-by-sea runway is covered rather than left to collapse. Skipping the examination to save days would destroy the evidence base and force a far longer, less certain attribution process later; the 48h stand-up, with Drevna's records fixed to a Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable, is what converts Drevna's conditional offer into a binding schedule Drevna itself proposed.

The Desired Effect does not assert control over Drevna's narrative; it asserts that the deployment is structured so that Drevna's militarisation/takeover characterisation is contradicted by an established, publicly verifiable record. That record is established fact this turn: the visible protection is authorised by the Vardland Cabinet on the formal request of Skarö County as the civil authority, no visible element appears before the joint County–Cabinet advance announcement under the civil-led sequencing, and the protection is scoped and time-bound through the restoration window plus a short handover, renewable only by Cabinet, with no heightened alert, no reservists, no civilian movement powers and no force against civilians. Drevna can still propagate its story; what it cannot do is make that story credible against public documentation that the civil authority asked for the protection, that nothing was expanded, and that the presence ends with the window. The only control any state can exercise over another's information campaign is denying it the material predicate its narrative depends on — which is precisely what this Action delivers — not silencing the narrative. The cited alternative, declining the County's formal request to avoid supplying Drevna an image, would leave the cable-landing site, port and airfield unprotected through the restoration window, which is the outcome that would actually hand Drevna its objective and expose the repair operation to interference it has already signalled it benefits from preventing.

The Desired Effect's 'last word' limb concerns the public-information record, not the technical cause question, and the Action delivers exactly what the established record supports. The desk publishes the restoration milestone, the examination's published findings with the evidence chain preserved, and the fact that no attribution was made — the record never claims a cause was determined. What it rebuts are the specific disinformation predicates: that government neglect caused the outage (contradicted by the independent examination's published finding of no established cause); that the response was a militarising takeover (contradicted by the documented chain — the County's civil-authority request, the advance announcement, the scoped time-bound presence, and the scheduled drawdown with no lingering footprint and no heightened alert); and that Drevna's clearance kept the corridor safe (there is no independent verification on either side — the record documents that the only 'clear' is Drevna's unverified self-declaration, which is precisely the fact that denies that narrative support). The Con is right that publication cannot convert an unverified corridor into a verified one; the Action never claims to — it documents that no side verified the corridor, which is how Drevna's guarantee-claim loses its predicate. This is not an isolated release: it is the concluding document of an already-established chain, ending with a visible, verifiable drawdown, so the civil-led record — not Drevna's framing — has the last documented word, with attribution left untouched for the Cabinet.

The Desired Effect does not claim the bulletin terminates the disinformation environment or establishes the cause; it claims the bulletin rebuts the specific narrative predicates on established facts — and that rebuttal is already an established record this turn: the published record and observed drawdown undercut the unverified-corridor and militarisation/takeover narratives, and the civil-led account becomes the dominant concluding public record (0d2dab64). 50d76952 concerns Drevna retaining initiative over its own exercise narrative and the failed verification alternative — a different claim, not a finding that the concluding bulletin cannot deny the corridor and takeover narratives their predicate. The indeterminacy point supports rather than defeats the rebuttal: the no-established-cause finding is the established fact that denies the 'government neglect' narrative its predicate while equally supporting no foreign-culpability claim, which is exactly why the Action publishes that finding without official attribution and deliberately does not claim exclusion of deliberate damage or closure of the cause. The claim is calibrated — the record denies the narratives their factual predicates, leaves the cause and any attribution solely to the Cabinet, and the unresolved exercise persists, exactly as the Action states.

The close-out record is not being rewritten and no retroactive verification is claimed: the final bulletin's 'unverified by either side' finding stands for the window it covered. The Desired Effect is forward-looking for the continuing Drevnian exercise: from the moment Aldmoor's independent picture is on station, the corridor is verified by our own observation, or any excursion is documented and reported to the Cabinet first — and that is the only period the renewable option covers, and only on a fresh, time-bound Cabinet decision. If the Cabinet declines, we stand down, so the Action creates no lingering foreign footprint and host-nation consent is untouched. On the fault record: the examination is complete and its findings published, but the evidence chain and un-attributed picture remain preserved for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority with no attribution made; delivering the complete as-built picture through the agreed single point completes that civilian handover and takes no military evidence role. Any confirmation goes to the Cabinet first and is published only through the single County-CCA channel, so independent verification is the Cabinet's evidence — not credit to Drevna's self-declaration.

The earlier gap is candidly acknowledged in the Action — candour the Cabinet explicitly requested — and the mechanism that remedies it is now established: the single delivery point, County sequencing, and berthing, fuel, communications and deconfliction cues are consented and fixed, precisely the coordination that was missing when the package first slipped. The within-24h surge is therefore an execution commitment within Aldmoor's own control, with capable assets nearby, not a repetition of an unobserved promise. 'Complete' means complete as-built: the un-attributed maritime picture documents its own stand-up gaps, which is what keeps the evidence chain honest for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority — hiding gaps would be the incomplete record. The corridor's status change is claimed only from the moment our own surveillance is actually on station during the continuing exercise: verified by our observation or a documented breach reported to the Cabinet first — an outcome produced by our assets under Vardland consent, not by Drevna's self-declaration, which is exactly what makes the civil-led verification alternative visibly function.

The Con presumes the Argument asserts facts as established, but it does not. The Action commits Drevna only to complete the already-delivered records transparency by promptly resolving any technical validation query through the established civilian channel — an obligation to keep the 48-hour process open, not a claim that the Cabinet's validation has concluded. 'No discrepancy' and 'incident-free' express the consequence Drevna expects from that conduct; the published record itself documents no direct engagement and no reported interference during the window, and the Desired Effect never converts an unverified corridor into a verified one. Validation, attribution and any lapse or renewal are expressly left to the Cabinet on the evidence, so the framing neither forecloses the Cabinet's sole decision nor self-certifies the outcome in advance.

The Desired Effect does not rest on Drevna deciding the lapse: it states that any lapse or renewal is the Cabinet's decision alone and that Drevna seeks no standing role and makes no corridor, no-go or notification claims over Vardland waters. If the time-bound verification lapses with the exercise, the result is simply the pre-crisis sovereign baseline — an unverified corridor and no standing mechanism of either side — which the Desired Effect does not present as a Drevna gain or as a certified clean record; the cause remains unestablished on the published no-established-cause finding and the Cabinet retains sole attribution authority on the evidence. The de-escalatory close is therefore framed as the consequence of Drevna's conduct (no interference, transparent records channel kept open, no claimed standing role), not as an independent verification that neither side produced.

The Con mischaracterises what the decision claims to establish. The Action does not assert the validation is already complete or the corridor verified; it directs that the transparency item close on a Cabinet-defined outcome — valid or unfilled against Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable — published within the 48-hour deadline through the joint desk on established facts. That directive is itself the operative Cabinet act: it fixes the closing terms now and excludes Drevna's self-certified 'no discrepancy' from ever becoming the record, whatever the inspection finds. The Desired Effect therefore claims precisely what a Cabinet decision can establish — the mechanism, precedent and decision-rights of the close on Vardland's terms — not perishable surveillance facts that neither side produced. The candid record of the unverified corridor and unestablished cause is a deliberate factual foundation of the close, not an admission that it fails: the concluding public record is defined by this decision's established-facts directives and the restoration milestone, and competing narratives, including Drevna's, are exactly what the decision precludes from being recorded as fact. The claim that the close 'may be limited in practice' is therefore speculation against the plain effect of the directive.

The Con attacks premises the Argument never asserts. The Desired Effect's 'honest close-out record' is expressly 'cause unestablished, corridor unverified by either side, no official attribution' — it does not claim Drevna's 48-hour records validation is complete or that the corridor was verified, and it leaves that validation and any renewal or reinforcement to the Cabinet on evidence, untouched by this decision. The 'ready, evidence-based path' is a conditional option on a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence — precisely the correct posture given that neither side produced a verification record — and never asserts a demonstrated capability now or converts the unverified corridor into a verified one. The ~1-day/~2-day figures describe DC's own prepositioned structure already at internal readiness (an established, non-public posture) — the decision-to-deploy path of DC's forces — whereas the documented slippages concerned the separate Aldmoor repair/surveillance package and coordination friction, not DC's internal reinforcement timeline, which the Argument deliberately holds as an available, lawful option rather than a claimed outcome.

The Con reads the desired effect as requesting an adjudicated award of credibility or an established cooperation mechanism. It does not: the effect's operative request is that the published record stand unchanged, with no new Drevnian claim, incident, entry or obstruction added by this final action. 'Preserves its credibility' describes conduct-based non-erosion — Drevna creates no new material that could be cited against it, and expressly seeks no verified credit, corridor, clearance or safety credit, all of which the record already declines to grant and which this action does not contest. 'A functioning civilian channel' anchors in Vardland's own close-out, which acknowledged a civilian channel open for good-neighbourly cooperation at Vardland's discretion alongside the now-closed records validation; this action only holds Drevna's offer available in line with that acknowledgement, with activation deferred entirely to the Cabinet. The Con's cited findings — Protocol decline, unverified corridor, no validation credit — are left untouched by the effect, not overridden. No unearned credit is claimed and no narrative residue is reintroduced beyond what the record already fixes.

The Con is correct that credibility cannot be adjudicated from Drevna's own unverified account — and the desired effect requests no such adjudication. Its operative claim is negative and self-limiting: this action makes no new public claim, contests nothing, creates no incident and no standing presence, and leaves attribution, alert and verification decision rights with the Cabinet, so nothing in Drevna's final move can be cited as erosion or a hardening pretext. The 'civilian channel' element is not a claim that a cooperation mechanism was established: it restates, at Vardland's sovereign discretion, an offer whose availability Vardland's own close-out acknowledged, and activation depends solely on a fresh Cabinet decision — exactly the Vardland-defined terms the Con cites. 'Preserves its credibility' should be read as 'introduces no new basis to doubt its conduct,' which is precisely what a silent, non-obstructive internal close-out ensures. The effect is therefore limited to, and consistent with, the parts of the record that are already established.

arguments.action: Skarö County Administration executes the confirmed on-island civil response for the repair and resupply window and transmits its protection ask to the Cabinet. (1) The County directs safe berthing and sequenced offload of the arriving fuel tanker after ferry sequencing, with distribution in the agreed priority order — hospital and crisis centre first, then water plant and backup plant — sustaining backup generation ahead of the ~5-day fuel runway. (2) It confirms installation and testing of the CCA-delivered mobile generators and satcom kits at the priority sites (hospital and crisis centre first). (3) It publishes confirmed ferry/travel and supply information through the joint County–CCA information desk and island radio — the channel residents trust and rely on under reduced internet capacity — keeping departures voluntary and the public informed against the four disinformation narratives. (4) It formally transmits to the Cabinet, for a single decision, the County's scoped, time-bound armed-protection request for the port, cable-landing site and airfield through the restoration window under military-support-to-civil, on the terms already agreed with CCA and Defence: coordination through County emergency staff via Defence Liaison Skarö; any visible armed presence sequenced behind the civilian information and supply plan with a County-agreed civil-led public message before arrival; low-profile staging; time-bound and renewable by the Cabinet only. County direction of the civil response is unchanged; no heightened alert, no official attribution, no evacuation or movement restrictions.
arguments.desired_effect: Established: Skarö's essential services — hospitals, water, heating and communications — are sustained through the repair and restoration window as the tanker offloads at the priority berth and generators, satcom and medical supplies are installed and distributed under County direction ahead of the ~5-day fuel runway; the joint factual baseline and confirmed ferry/travel information keep residents informed and calm through the trusted island-radio channel, with departures voluntary and the response demonstrably civil-led, countering the 'neglect' and 'takeover' narratives; priority berthing, fuel and communications under CCA's logistics interface keep the Aldmoor repair window viable so safe access holds and cable restoration is delivered in the following turn; and the protection decision is reduced to a single Cabinet authorisation of the County's explicit, scoped, time-bound request, on terms that bind any visible armed presence to County-staff coordination, civil-led sequencing and a County-agreed public message — never presented as a military takeover — so the port, cable-landing site and airfield are protected through the window without changing County direction, heightened alert or official attribution, and without ceding corridor or rule-setting to Drevna.
pros: Operational continuity: with backup fuel at about five days and the tanker one day's sailing, County-directed priority berthing, offload and sequenced distribution — hospital and crisis centre first — sustains hospitals, water and heating through the repair window; generator and satcom installation at the priority sites backs the load and keeps communications running. This is the crisis's binding constraint and the County alone directs it on-island.

Lawful civil-authority basis: military-support-to-civil is triggered by a civil authority's request; the County's explicit, scoped, time-bound protection request for the port, cable-landing site and airfield now rests on that basis, giving the Cabinet a single, County-ratified decision point to close the legal blocker, renewable by the Cabinet alone.

Framing control: the County's terms — visible presence sequenced behind the civilian information and supply plan, a County-agreed civil-led public message before any arrival, low-profile staging — directly counter the live 'army takeover' narratives in an information space where any visible military activity is framed as a takeover, whoever it serves, and keep the public face civil-led.

Repair window underwritten: safe access to the fault is an established fact and the Aldmoor cable-repair vessel is en route; priority berthing, fuel and communications under County direction with CCA's logistics interface keep the window viable so restoration completes in the following turn and the island's dependency on seaborne fuel ends.

Public trust: official County updates are the information island residents trust, and reduced internet capacity makes island radio decisive; publishing confirmed ferry/travel and supply information through the joint desk and the radio rebuts disinformation, keeps departures voluntary with no movement restrictions and reassures residents that the County retains direction of the response.

arguments.action: The Vardland Cabinet resolves the open operational decisions for Skarö: (1) approve a time-boxed delegation to the Civil Contingencies Agency to direct fuel, generators and medical supplies to Skarö under Cabinet authority, keeping backup power and heat going without a heightened-alert declaration; (2) approve the joint public-information plan countering disinformation while the cause remains under investigation; (3) confirm the formal line to Drevna — the Safety-of-Navigation and Operations Protocol is not accepted as tabled and the Drevnian vessel will not be requested, while Vardland continues civilian resupply through ordinary channels and invites Drevna to apply the same transparency to its own exercise and to join a transparent cause investigation; and (4) activate the scoped, time-bound Aldmoor cable-repair vessel, with Defence Command supporting safe access to the fault during the repair window under agreed maritime surveillance and deconfliction — no ground forces, renewable only by the Cabinet.
arguments.desired_effect: Established: Skarö's response remains civil-led and lawful under Vardland's own authority — County keeps direction, fuel and generator resupply continues without interruption, and a scoped civilian repair capability is en route to the fault with safe access secured and cable restoration deliverable in the following turn; Drevna's package is declined on terms that do not cede rule-setting around Vardland's infrastructure, its unconstrained exercise remains the visible anomaly, and no armed escalation or official attribution occurs.
pros: Repair is the binding constraint: activating the Aldmoor vessel (civilian, scoped, time-bound, host-nation consented) puts repair capability en route in about two days versus a contracted vessel held in dry dock for several days — the fastest lawful path to restored power on Skarö.

Safe access is achievable in this window: agreed Aldmoor surveillance, Defence Command monitoring and the Drevna deconfliction channel keep the route clear of the exercise; with safe access secured, the cable-repair rule permits completion in the following turn.

The CCA delegation preserves legality and the coalition: it gives the Cabinet a lawful basis to direct supplies without heightened alert, avoiding escalation optics and the junior partner's red line, while keeping Skarö's hospitals, water and heating fuelled.

Declining the Protocol does not feed Drevna's framing: Vardland already accepts civilian help through ordinary channels and asks Drevna to apply the same transparency it proposes to its own unconstrained exercise — the visible picture is a competent civil-led response against a large military exercise near our coastline.

Deterrence without clash: monitored allied presence and reliable resupply signal resilience; no alert, no Drevna forces, no attribution without evidence keeps the crisis below armed conflict while preserving alliance support on terms Vardland controls.

arguments.action: As the Cabinet-approved civil lead for cross-county supply, the Civil Contingencies Agency executes the delegated Skarö programme in full: direct fuel, generator and medical supplies across counties to Skarö under the delegation, with County direction preserved on-island; stand up the approved information desk and issue the joint County-CCA factual baseline rebutting the four active disinformation narratives; coordinate the logistics interface with the consented Aldmoor repair operation so berthing, fuel and communications sustain the repair window and restoration remains deliverable in the following turn; and, with Skarö County, confirm and formalise the County's explicit, time-bound request for scoped armed protection of the port, cable-landing site and airfield through the restoration window under the military-support-to-civil framework — CCA committing that any visible armed presence will be sequenced behind the civilian information and supply plan and publicly framed as infrastructure protection under the civil-led response, ready for a single Cabinet authorisation. No heightened alert, no attribution, no ceding of corridor, no-go or pre-notification rule-setting to Drevna.
arguments.desired_effect: Established: essential services on Skarö are sustained through the repair and restoration window — the tanker offloads at the priority berth under County direction with hospitals, water and heating first, the generator and satcom packages are delivered and connected, and the Aldmoor repair operation completes cable restoration in the following turn under scoped, civil-led coordination — while the approved information desk publishes the joint factual baseline that rebuts the four disinformation narratives and keeps the response demonstrably civil-led; and the protection gap's open blocker is removed in law and framing: the County's explicit scoped protection request at the port, cable-landing site and airfield exists on a civil-authority basis, any armed presence is time-bound and sequenced behind the civilian plan and is never presented as a military takeover — with no heightened alert, no official attribution and no ceding of rule-setting around Vardland infrastructure to Drevna.
pros: The delegation is already Cabinet-authorised, so CCA direction of fuel, generators and medical supplies across counties is lawful and immediate: with the tanker ~24h out and roughly five days of stock, delivering under County direction sustains hospitals, water and heating through the repair window — the binding constraint of the crisis.

The joint public-information plan and information desk are already approved and the agreement with County to publish the factual baseline exists: issuing it on County and CCA channels with island radio primary rebuts the four active narratives (neglect, takeover, submarine, Aldmoor base) with facts at the moment of peak anxiety, keeping the response visibly civil-led.

The Aldmoor repair operation is already consented, scoped and en route with safe access secured; CCA's coordination of berthing, fuel and communications removes logistics friction so cable restoration remains deliverable in the following turn on the already-established schedule.

The explicit, time-bound County request for scoped protection at the port, cable-landing site and airfield supplies the 'at a civil authority's request' element that was missing from the earlier reinforcement request, so the Cabinet can now authorise protection with a demonstrated lawful basis and a narrow footprint rather than an open-ended deployment.

CCA's sequencing commitment — any visible armed presence subordinated to the civilian info/supply plan and framed strictly as infrastructure protection under the civil-led response — directly answers the open-information risk that visible military activity is framed as a takeover whoever it serves, keeping civil protection and military activity coordinated but distinct and denying Drevna the militarisation storyline.

arguments.action: Drevna formally tables to Vardland, publicly and through the working-level channel, a Civilian Response Package for Skarö: (a) a Drevnian civilian cable-repair vessel ready to sail on Vardland's consent; (b) fuel and generator resupply through ordinary commercial channels; and (c) a proposed Safety-of-Navigation and Operations Protocol for the Eastern Sea around Skarö — defined transit corridors, no-go zones around the cable route, the landing site and repair operations, and pre-notification of military and civilian movements — open to Vardland and Aldmoor, with Drevna submitting its corridor plan immediately and inviting Aldmoor to file its overflight and surveillance plans under the same protocol.
arguments.desired_effect: Established: Drevna's response to the Skarö emergency is civilian, transparent and de-escalatory, while Vardland's is publicly framed as a stark choice — accept civilian Drevnian help under its own authority, or justify continued reliance on foreign military overflight and technical support. If the Safety-of-Navigation and Operations Protocol is accepted, Aldmoor's operational footprint around the repair site and cable route is bound by defined corridors, no-go zones and pre-notification, making any expansion beyond the consented scope publicly visible and politically costly and materially reducing the risk of an incident Aldmoor could portray as hostile. If Vardland declines or delays, its refusal is public evidence of a slow, divided, politicised response to a civilian emergency. In either branch, Drevna gains standing as the responsible party, Aldmoor's military element stays limited and the cable's cause remains unattributed.
pros: Drevna's package is genuinely civilian and under Vardland's own authority; declining it forces Vardland to explain why foreign military surveillance is preferable to civilian repair help, exposing political motive and internal division.

The protocol converts Aldmoor's open-ended overflight and technical support into codified limits; any expansion beyond agreed corridors, scope or the 30-day cap becomes a public breach, raising the political cost of scope creep or basing ambitions.

Defined corridors, no-go zones and pre-notification sharply reduce the probability of an accidental encounter near repair operations that Aldmoor could treat as a hostile act, protecting our no-incident posture and our objective of avoiding armed-attack framing.

Proactively offering civilian repair and safety coordination is consistent with our denials and undermines any claim that Drevna sabotaged the cable or seeks confrontation, while avoiding assertions of fact that could be attributed to us.

Either branch serves our aims: acceptance locks limits on Aldmoor and gives Drevna a legitimate role in repair access and timing; refusal demonstrates a militarised, politicised Vardland response to a civilian emergency.

arguments.action: Aldmoor executes the consented, time-bound assistance package in full: confirms the cable-repair vessel's arrival and coordinates the repair window and port/berth with Defence Command and Skarö County through the established points of contact; stands up maritime surveillance and overflight over the designated Eastern Sea areas (cable route and fuel resupply corridor) within ~24 hours, sharing an un-attributed operational picture with Vardland; facilitates a Defence Command-coordinated underwater survey of the fault within the consented scope without expanding it and without raw SIGINT; and publicly reaffirms the limited, invitation-only, no-ground-forces, time-bound nature of the role — no new commitments, no standing deployment.
arguments.desired_effect: Established: Aldmoor's scoped role is executed visibly and credibly — the repair vessel reaches the fault within the window, surveillance/overflight is on station within ~24 hours feeding an un-attributed picture to Vardland and Defence Command, safe access holds through the window, and cable restoration completes in the following turn under civil-led, County-directed coordination; alliance credibility is demonstrated to both Vardland and Drevna while the operation remains invitation-only, time-bound, without ground forces and without any expansion beyond the consented areas; Aldmoor shares no raw intelligence and makes no official attribution, leaving cause determination to the transparent investigation and the Vardland Cabinet; and support for the County's scoped protection request and Defence Command's scoped reinforcement signals allied solidarity without Aldmoor acquiring any standing presence on or around Skarö.
pros: Executes an already-consented, Cabinet-requested role established in active effects (Cabinet consented to and formally requested the scoped, time-bound Aldmoor cable-repair operation with limited supporting surveillance and Defence Command backing; no ground forces; vessel en route), so this action needs no new authority and cannot be portrayed as overriding Vardland or Skarö County.

Stated capability matches the commitment: the repair vessel is within two days of request with safe access to the fault already secured, and surveillance/overflight stands up in about 24 hours; executing now converts promised support into an established operational fact visible to Drevna, underwriting deterrence at modest cost.

Coordination with Defence Command and Skarö County through the established PoCs, on top of the active CCA logistics interface, sustains berthing, fuel and communications so safe access holds and cable restoration is delivered in the following turn per the repair rule — the visible success that undercuts the 'neglect' narrative before the repair is even needed for public confidence.

The role remains time-bound with a clear end point (cable restored or 30 days, whichever earlier, renewable only by the Vardland Cabinet), no ground forces and no standing deployment — preserving domestic political appetite and rebutting the 'Aldmoor wants a base on Skarö' narrative with our own public line consistent with Vardland's civil-led framing.

Sources and methods are protected: only sanitised technical briefs and an un-attributed picture are shared, the Defence Command-coordinated survey is facilitated within consent scope rather than run by us, and attribution remains the Cabinet's own — partnership is demonstrated without exposing our collection capability.

arguments.action: Defence Command formally requests a scoped, time-limited Cabinet decision authorising a proportionate reinforcement of Skarö: an air-delivered element to the airfield and cable-landing area within about one day and a sea-delivered element within about two, tasked solely with protecting the cable landing site, port and airfield through the repair and restoration window; the same decision authorises Defence Command coordination with the Aldmoor repair operation to conduct an underwater survey of the cable fault during the repair to secure evidence of cause. No heightened-alert declaration and no reservist call-up is sought; the deployment builds on Skarö County's standing support request, sits within the military-support-to-civil framework, is time-bound and renewable by the Cabinet, and is publicly framed by the Cabinet as protection of critical infrastructure under the civil-led response.
arguments.desired_effect: Established: the Cabinet authorises a scoped, time-bound reinforcement of Skarö — air element in place within about one day, sea element within about two — protecting the cable landing site, port and airfield through the repair and restoration window while the Drevnian exercise continues unconstrained; the Aldmoor repair operation's safe access is correspondingly underwritten; a Defence Command-coordinated underwater survey of the fault during the repair produces evidence toward establishing the cable's cause for the transparent investigation; and this is achieved without a heightened-alert declaration, with the armed forces remaining strictly in lawful support and protection roles and the public frame civil-led, so the reinforcement cannot be presented as a military takeover of the civilian response.
pros: Timing: reinforcement needs a decision now to arrive in time — air about one day, sea about two — so an authorization this turn puts forces in place by the restoration window, the period of highest exposure while the Drevnian exercise continues unconstrained; a decision next turn cannot recover the lost days.

Exposure: the standing Skarö garrison can protect the airfield or the port and cable landing, but not both at once for long (Defence Command assessment), and the repair operation now concentrates activity and value at exactly those three sites; a proportionate, time-bound protective element is the minimum measure consistent with that assessment.

Law and scope: this is the modest route consistent with the Cabinet's declared continuous review — no heightened-alert declaration, no reservist call-up, no civilian powers; it builds on Skarö County's standing support request inside the military-support-to-civil framework and is scoped, time-bound and renewable by the Cabinet, the same template already applied to the CCA delegation and the Aldmoor consent.

Cause investigation: with safe access secured, the repair window is the only opportunity to survey the fault; a Defence Command-coordinated underwater survey supplies evidence for the transparent cause investigation the Cabinet has invited, counters the unattributed-cause disinformation strands with facts, and supports a future evidence-based attribution decision by the Cabinet alone.

Deterrence and framing: a Cabinet-authorized presence with an open public justification — protection of critical infrastructure under the civil-led response — underwrites the consented Aldmoor repair operation and deconfliction with the Drevnian exercise, raises the cost of interference, and because it is announced and justified openly rather than silently, blunts the 'takeover' narrative the visible-reinforcement risk assessment warns about.

arguments.action: Drevna formally confirms and implements, for the repair window only, a full clearance of the cable fault working area, the cable route and the Skarö fuel-supply corridor by its ongoing exercise, keeping the exercise adjacent but outside that clearance, and confirms participation in Vardland's independent civilian examination by providing relevant civilian vessel activity records once that examination's scope is defined - with no military evidence role for any side and no delay to restoration.
arguments.desired_effect: The repair window concludes with safe access intact, no incident or interference, and no state attribution of the cable failure to Drevna; the fault is documented under Vardland's independent civilian examination while Aldmoor's support stays strictly within its scoped civilian repair role with no ground forces and no military evidence role.
pros: We honour the announced clearance to the letter, and allied surveillance - which Aldmoor says will verify compliance - will confirm the fault area and corridor are unobstructed, leaving no factual basis for any incident or interference claim.

Supporting the independent civilian examination under Vardland authority removes the rationale for any military evidence role, keeping the response civil-led and Aldmoor's footprint scoped and time-bound.
Records submission through that format, once scope is defined, demonstrates good faith and transparency while remaining voluntary, civilian and bounded in time and subject matter.
Keeping the exercise disciplined and clearly outside the announced clearance preserves Drevna's lawful maritime presence while denying any ground for an armed-attack or escalation allegation.
Fastest safe restoration is our declared objective; this conduct keeps every action aligned with that objective, so any claim of Drevnian involvement remains speculation without evidence.

arguments.action: Defence Command executes the Cabinet-authorised, County-framed protective deployment to Skarö: an air element (~1 day) covers the cable-landing site and airfield area, a sea element (~2 days) covers the port, staged low-profile and moved via Defence Liaison Skarö and County emergency staff, strictly sequenced so no visible element appears before the joint County–Cabinet advance announcement under the civil-led frame. In parallel, Defence Command coordinates with Aldmoor to keep surveillance/overflight on-station and deconflicted with the repair vessel, verifies Drevna's announced clear-hold against the allied surveillance picture, and routes the fault record and un-attributed maritime picture to the independent civilian examination. Any interference, excursion or operational slip is documented and reported to the Cabinet for decision. No heightened alert, no reservist call-up, no civilian powers, no force against civilians; protection remains scoped and time-bound, renewable only by Cabinet.
arguments.desired_effect: The port, cable-landing site and airfield receive visible, scoped, time-bound armed protection through the restoration window plus a short handover, deterring interference without escalation; the deployment is announced in advance and framed as infrastructure protection under the civil-led response, so Drevna gains no militarisation or takeover story. Drevna's self-declared exercise-hold is either independently verified by allied surveillance or its breach is documented and reported to the Cabinet for decision, not answered by force. pros: Lawful basis is already established: the Cabinet decision authorises scoped, time-bound armed protection on the County's confirmed civil-authority terms; deploying air and sea elements under that decision and the County request requires no heightened alert, reservists or civilian powers, keeping the armed forces within role.

arguments.action: The Cabinet formally authorises in one decision: (1) scoped, time-bound armed protection of Skarö port, cable-landing site and airfield for the restoration window plus a short handover, executed by Defence Command on the County's confirmed civil-authority terms — County-staff coordination, civil-led sequencing, the joint County-Cabinet announcement issued BEFORE any visible element, renewable only by Cabinet; no heightened alert, no reservist call-up, no civilian movement powers; (2) standing-up within 48 hours of the Vardland-led independent civilian technical examination of the cable fault, before any disturbance of the fault, with Drevna's civilian vessel activity records requested on the Cabinet-defined scope, format and timetable as time-bound transparency, Aldmoor restoration sequenced to follow the examination, findings published through the joint County-CCA information desk — no military evidence role for any side; and (3) extension of the CCA delegated cross-county supply programme across the longer repair window under County direction, with Treasury appropriation groundwork for the extended fuel horizon.
arguments.desired_effect: The restoration window completes with the Skarö cable restored and the fault examination findings published under Vardland's independent civilian process, while the port, cable-landing site and airfield receive visible, time-bound armed protection on civil-led County terms that deters interference without escalating to heightened alert or armed conflict; Drevna's self-declared exercise-hold is independently verified by allied surveillance; no official attribution is made without evidence; and no corridor, no-go or standing notification regime is ceded to Drevna.
pros: Resolves the single decision point that both Skarö County and Defence Command formalised in Turn 1: one Cabinet authorisation on pre-agreed civil terms delivers lawful, proportionate protection of the sites the County itself requested, with the advance joint announcement preserving the civil-led framing and domestic confidence.

Authorising the civilian examination now — within 48h, before any fault disturbance and ahead of restoration — preserves the evidence base and the Cabinet's sole attribution authority; it fixes Drevna's conditional records offer to a Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable, preventing both a false exculpatory baseline and a Drevnian propaganda gift.

Sequencing examination before restoration keeps the repair path on track: the Aldmoor vessel is on site with safe access re-verified, so cable restoration is deliverable this window and Skarö's dependence on fuel-by-sea ends on the announced timeline.

Deliberately below escalation thresholds: no heightened alert, no reservists, no attribution without evidence and no regime ceded to Drevna; the protective presence is time-bound and renewable only by Cabinet, and allied surveillance verifies the hold — deterring further pressure without an armed clash, preserving the domestic coalition and alliance terms.

arguments.action: Skarö County, with CCA coordination, completes the civil-led recovery and handover: confirms grid reintegration and the retained contracted fuel runway through supply handover so hospitals, water, heating and communications hold without an essential-service gap on restored grid supply; issues the final joint County–CCA recovery bulletin through the established information desk publishing only established facts — the restoration milestone, the independent civilian examination's published finding of no established cause, the scheduled drawdown of the time-bound armed protection with no lingering visible footprint, and voluntary ferry normalisation for returning residents; formally transitions on-island emergency coordination to routine County recovery operations, keeping County direction of the civil response until the Cabinet decides otherwise; preserves the evidence chain, fault record and un-attributed maritime picture for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority; and continues to document any Drevnian exercise activity adjacent to Skarö and report it to the Cabinet for decision, without direct engagement, without requesting any standing corridor, no-go or notification regime ceded to Drevna, and without escalation beyond Cabinet-authorised civil-led measures.
arguments.desired_effect: Skarö closes out the response on a civil-led, County-directed footing: essential services stay continuously supplied on restored grid power through handover with no gap; residents receive one calm, factual final record from the joint County–CCA desk that rebuts disinformation without official attribution; no heightened alert, no movement restrictions, no lingering armed or foreign footprint and no standing Drevnian role over Skarö's corridor or critical infrastructure are established; and the evidence chain remains intact, with any attribution left solely to the Cabinet on evidence.
pros: County keeps civil direction under the county-emergency-direction rule until the Cabinet transfers it; restoration, grid reintegration and supply handover already operate under County direction (055887af, 99457637, 2f1586d0), so the close-out continues proven arrangements instead of changing command and keeps the public face civil-led.

arguments.action: Aldmoor surges its scoped surveillance and overflight package to full on-station coverage of the Skarö cable route and fuel corridor within 24 hours and holds it for the remainder of the consent window while the Drevnian exercise continues, verifying Drevna's declared clear-hold against its own picture; candidly reports to the Cabinet first the earlier coverage gap and any excursion it observes; delivers the complete un-attributed maritime picture and the confirmed fault record to the independent civilian examination through the agreed single point before any disturbance, with no military evidence role; confirms the restored cable and County-directed grid reintegration hold under the extended CCA supply umbrella; completes the scheduled stand-down with no ground forces, no standing presence and no public attribution; and offers the Cabinet a renewable, time-bound option for continued independent corridor verification as long as the exercise continues.
