Restoration sequencing is already fixed by the Cabinet decision - examination before any disturbance - and our vessel is on site with access secured; the confirmed restoration and County-directed grid reintegration therefore hold within the CCA-extended supply runway without any scope expansion or new authorisation.

arguments.action: Defence Command, without public announcement and strictly within its lawful role, preserves the evidence chain and the un-attributed fault record for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority; keeps the Skarö garrison at internal readiness; keeps reinforcement (air ~1 day, sea ~2 days after a decision) and a renewable, time-bound corridor-verification option available only on a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence; and supports the joint County-CCA civil-led transition to routine winter-resilience monitoring at civil request - with no standing allied presence, no corridor/no-go/notification regime ceded to Drevna, no heightened alert and no public DC messaging.

arguments.action: The Civil Contingencies Agency completes the Cabinet-directed technical inspection of Drevna's vessel-activity records against the Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable, and publishes the outcome — valid, or unfilled — through the joint County–CCA information desk on established facts within the 48-hour deadline; reports the finding to the Cabinet first; transitions the stand-down of emergency logistics into the joint County–CCA winter-resilience programme (island fuel reserve, generator rotation and refresh, backup communications, drilled offload-and-sequencing) under County direction with CCA supply coordination and Treasury-costed support; keeps the standby information-desk protocol armed so any new disinformation surge or infrastructure event re-activates the joint desk to rebut with the published close-out record only; and preserves the evidence chain with no official attribution, no retroactive validation of Drevna's clear-hold, and no standing foreign presence.

arguments.action: Drevna conducts an orderly, incident-free conclusion of the naval and air exercise on its published schedule, strictly in international spaces and fully respecting the declared clearance boundary, while completing its already-delivered civilian vessel-activity records transparency by promptly resolving any technical validation query through the established civilian channel, and makes no corridor, no-go or notification claims over Vardland waters.

arguments.action: The Cabinet, acting on established facts, decides the close of the Skarö response on Vardland's terms: it directs the CCA technical inspection of Drevna's vessel-activity records to completion and publication of the outcome — valid or unfilled against the Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable — through the joint County–CCA information desk within the 48-hour deadline; it decides that the time-bound allied corridor verification concludes with the Drevnian exercise as a deliberate Cabinet decision, with Aldmoor standing down leaving no standing presence and no further elements; it records candidly that the corridor remained unverified by either side through the window and that the cable's cause remains unestablished under the published no-established-cause finding, with official attribution and any future verification renewal remaining the Cabinet's sole decisions on evidence; and it directs the transition to routine civil-led monitoring and winter-resilience implementation under the joint County–CCA framework.
arguments.desired_effect: The crisis concludes de-escalated on Vardland-authored terms: the vessel-records transparency item closes on the Cabinet's established-facts finding, not Drevna's self-reported 'no discrepancy'; corridor verification ends as the Cabinet's sovereign decision on documented facts, not Drevna's asserted 'natural lapse', so no standing Drevnian or allied mechanism survives and renewal remains the Cabinet's alone on evidence; the corridor's unverified status and the unresolved cause are honestly recorded, so Drevna gains no unearned safety credit and no official attribution is made by any side; and the civil-led account, the restoration milestone and the forward resilience programme stand as the concluding public record.
pros: Closing the records item on our established-facts finding — valid or unfilled against Vardland-defined scope within the 48-hour deadline — enforces our validation discipline and prevents Drevna from converting its self-reported 'no discrepancy' into the record.

Concluding verification as an explicit Cabinet decision on documented facts, rather than Drevna's asserted 'natural lapse', preserves the precedent that any standing or renewed mechanism exists only by Vardland's grant, renewable solely by the Cabinet on evidence.

Candidly recording that the corridor was never independently verified by either side and that the cause remains unestablished denies Drevna unearned corridor-safety credit and keeps official attribution exclusively with the Cabinet.

Standing down allied verification with no standing presence forestalls a Drevnian 'foreign footprint' narrative and dependence optics while keeping alliance support renewable on terms the Cabinet controls.

Anchoring the close in restoration and the joint County–CCA resilience programme keeps the civil-led, lawful national authority visibly credible as the concluding record and prepares Skarö against future outages without escalation.

arguments.action: Under the Cabinet's express close-out decision, Aldmoor completes and certifies its final mandated act: it delivers its final on-station and observation record through the agreed single point into the Cabinet evidence file; confirms in writing to the Cabinet that no Aldmoor elements remain on Vardland territory, in its territorial waters or in its airspace and that its time-bound role concluded with the Drevnian exercise; abstains from all public commentary and from any role in the CCA validation of Drevna's vessel-activity records; withholds raw SIGINT to protect sources and methods; and leaves no standing presence, holding only a renewable, time-bound corridor-verification option that would require a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence.
arguments.desired_effect: Alliance credibility is consolidated on the honest close: the record fixes that Aldmoor executed the scoped, time-bound consent package (cable-repair support and corridor surveillance) on the Cabinet's conditions, delivered its final record to the Cabinet's evidence file, and departed completely with no standing presence and no further elements; the 'Aldmoor base/expansion' narrative is denied its factual predicate and Drevna gains no corridor, clearance or safety credit; the candid concluding record (cause unestablished, corridor unverified by either side, no official attribution) stands without any Aldmoor public commentary; Vardland's sole decision-rights over attribution, verification renewal and any future presence are respected; Aldmoor's intelligence sources and methods remain protected; and any future verification remains a time-bound option awaiting a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence.
pros: Established facts already carry most of the substance - the Cabinet concluded corridor verification by express decision as the exercise ended, with Aldmoor standing down, no standing presence and no further elements (eefd054e; b96ea7ec; 5016b1df) - so this Argument fixes Aldmoor's final acts (record delivery, certified departure) as explicit adjudicated facts rather than inference.

Delivering the final on-station and observation record through the agreed single point honours the Cabinet's request and preserves the un-attributed picture, fault record and evidence chain for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority, consistent with Aldmoor's no-military-evidence-role and no-attribution commitments (06628a03; d14fc531; a83c443d).

Abstaining from public commentary and withholding raw SIGINT protects collection methods and keeps the joint County-CCA desk the single public channel, denying the militarisation/takeover and 'Aldmoor base' narratives their predicate while the civil-led close-out record stands (0d2dab64; 7782f006; 5016b1df).

The only mechanism offered is a renewable, time-bound verification option gated on a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence (eefd054e; d7882b08), so Aldmoor cannot be drawn into a standing deployment, presumes no renewal and fully respects host-nation consent and Cabinet decision-rights.

Executing the mandate exactly within scope and departing on schedule repairs the credibility dented by the earlier surveillance gap (ed97b1ed) and demonstrates to both Vardland and Drevna that allied commitment is reliable, bounded and end-dated - the strongest solidarity signal at the close.

arguments.action: The Cabinet issues its final crisis close-out decision: it adds no new claims and stands solely on the published established-facts record (cable restored and grid sustained under County-directed civil-led recovery; cause unestablished; corridor unverified by either side; no official attribution by any side; no standing foreign or Drevnian presence, corridor, no-go or notification regime). It retains the standby joint County-CCA information-desk protocol, the preserved un-attributed evidence chain and fault record, the private internal readiness of the Skarö garrison, and the renewable time-bound Aldmoor corridor-verification and Cabinet-gated reinforcement options, each requiring a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence, and confirms transition to the County-directed winter-resilience programme under the joint County-CCA framework, with any future Drevna civilian-channel approach considered only on Vardland-defined terms and a fresh Cabinet decision.
arguments.desired_effect: The crisis closes with the established-facts record standing as the conclusive public baseline: power and communications restored and sustained, cause unestablished, corridor unverified by either side, no official attribution by any side, and no standing foreign or Drevnian military presence, corridor, no-go or notification regime created. Recovery continues under County direction within the joint County-CCA winter-resilience framework; standby information-desk, evidence-chain and internal-readiness mechanisms remain armed for any recurrence; and attribution, alert, verification, any future foreign presence and any Drevna cooperation remain decision rights solely of the Vardland Cabinet on documented evidence, granting Drevna no credibility, safety or functioning-channel credit beyond the record.
pros: It cites only established facts already in the published record, so the close-out adds no new claim any actor can contest or exploit and leaves no fresh Drevnian narrative material.

It consolidates the coherent, fully Cabinet-gated recurrence posture (standby desk, preserved evidence chain, private garrison readiness, renewable verification and reinforcement options) that the turn-3 record recognises as ready, keeping national authority credible, lawful and visibly civil-led.

It keeps the crisis below war: no heightened alert, no attribution without evidence, no engagement with the concluded and departed Drevnian exercise, and no standing military presence that Drevna or domestic actors could frame as escalation or militarisation.

It preserves alliance support on terms Vardland controls: Aldmoor's renewable verification and reinforcement options remain available solely on a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence, with no ground forces and no standing presence, consistent with Aldmoor's written certification of departure.

It confirms County-directed civil-led recovery and winter-resilience that the island values, creates no Drevnian role over Skarö's corridor or critical infrastructure, and grants Drevna no credit for unverified self-reported conduct, consistent with the no-military-evidence-role and Cabinet-first rules.

arguments.action: Defence Command completes the final turn in silent, lawful readiness. It preserves the evidence chain and the un-attributed fault record for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority and issues no public Defence Command messaging. The Skarö garrison remains at unannounced internal readiness. No unit moves, no heightened alert, no reservist call-up, no movement powers and no force against civilians are ordered. The reinforcement and renewable time-bound corridor-verification options stay available but inert, each activated only by a fresh Cabinet decision on documented evidence. Defence Command stands ready to support the County-CCA winter-resilience programme at a civil authority's request under the military-support-to-civil rule, and to report any excursion or incident to the Cabinet first.
arguments.desired_effect: The final record closes with Defence Command's posture silent, lawful and fully Cabinet-gated: the evidence chain and un-attributed fault record stay preserved for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority; no armed escalation, standing military presence, corridor, no-go or notification regime or unearned Drevnian credit is created; the cable's cause remains unestablished and the corridor unverified by either side; and attribution, alert, verification renewal, foreign presence and any cooperation decisions remain the Cabinet's alone, to be made on documented evidence.
pros: Consistent with the Cabinet's T4 close-out and the adjudicated record: it adds no new claims, cites only established facts, and reserves all decision-rights to the Cabinet, keeping DC's disciplined line intact and denying Drevna any pretext.

Preserves the armed forces' lawful role: no heightened alert, call-up, movement powers or force against civilians; military support to the civil-led response occurs only at a civil authority's request, exactly as the law requires.

Denies Drevna any credit beyond the record: the corridor stays unverified by either side, the cause unestablished, and no Drevnian or standing allied mechanism survives the close, so no narrative residue is reintroduced.

Maintains genuine capability without escalation: private internal garrison readiness, Cabinet-gated reinforcement and the renewable verification option form a coherent recurrence-response posture, each activating only on a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence.

No public DC messaging or visible military footprint keeps the close-out visibly civil-led, consistent with the civil-frame established over the crisis and preventing any militarisation/takeover narrative.

arguments.action: Drevna takes its final crisis action as a restrained, internal close-out: it makes no new public statement and issues no new claims about the cable's cause, and it does not contest the published record. It confirms internally, and through the established civilian channel only if Vardland initiates, that its exercise concluded on schedule without incident and outside Vardland territory, territorial waters and airspace; that its vessel-activity records were delivered under Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable; and that its civilian cable-repair and good-neighbourhood cooperation offer remains available at Vardland's sovereign discretion, with attribution, alert and verification decision rights left entirely in the Vardland Cabinet.
arguments.desired_effect: The concluding public record stands without any change to Drevna's detriment: the cable's cause remains unestablished; no official attribution exists by any side; no standing foreign or Drevnian military presence, corridor, no-go or notification regime is created; Vardland's Cabinet retains sole decision authority on attribution, alert and verification; and Drevna preserves its credibility and a functioning civilian channel for any future good-neighbourly cooperation.
pros: Restraint matches the confirmed record: no new claims, no re-litigation, no obstruction, so nothing can be cited as a Drevnian escalation, inconsistency or hardening pretext.
Full respect for Vardland's sole attribution and decision authority removes the predicate for an evidence-backed attribution or for durable anti-Drevna consensus.
Holding the civilian cooperation offer open at Vardland's sovereign discretion preserves long-game standing value without allowing the offer to be framed as pressure or a corridor claim.
The action creates no incident, interference or entry into Vardland territory, territorial waters or airspace, preserving the no-armed-attack-predicate objective.
Silence on the unresolved cause protects the deniability posture of the survey vessel and directed accounts, leaving the no-established-cause finding as the only public baseline.

arguments.action: Aldmoor completes its final stand-down and closes out its involvement: through the agreed single point it confirms to the Vardland Cabinet that no Aldmoor elements remain on Vardland territory, territorial waters or airspace; it safeguards the delivered un-attributed on-station and observation record and withholds raw SIGINT to protect sources and methods; it issues no public commentary; and it holds the renewable, time-bound corridor-verification option available solely for a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence.
arguments.desired_effect: The crisis closes with the published established-facts record standing unchanged on Vardland terms: the cable restored under County-directed civil-led recovery, the cause unestablished, the corridor unverified by either side, no official attribution by any side, no standing foreign or Drevnian military presence and no corridor, no-go or notification regime, with all decision rights - attribution, alert, verification renewal, foreign presence and any cooperation - remaining solely with the Vardland Cabinet. Aldmoor's alliance-credibility objective is met through a scoped, consent-based contribution that was executed, completed and fully departed on schedule, with no standing deployment and no unearned credit to Drevna.
pros: Fully aligned with the closing record: every turn-4 close-out (Cabinet, CCA, Skaroe County, Defence Command, Drevna) ends on the same civil-led, Cabinet-gated baseline; Aldmoor's silent completion adds nothing and contests nothing, protecting the consensus end-state.

Credibility demonstrated by execution and departure: the scoped, time-limited operation was delivered and stood down in writing through the agreed single point, exactly matching the host-nation-consent terms and confirming no presence remains.
Sources and methods protected: only the consolidated un-attributed observation record was shared; raw SIGINT remains withheld, consistent with the intelligence-protection constraint.
No standing deployment: the renewable corridor-verification option passes to a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence; no base, no lingering footprint and no open-ended commitment is created.
Drevna gains no credit and no corridor mechanism: the unverified-corridor and no-established-cause findings stand as published, and every decision right remains with the Cabinet.

arguments.action: CCA completes its civil-led close-out strictly within the established record: it delivers the agreed pre-reads to Skarö County for the early-October winter-resilience working session, maintains the joint County-CCA standby information desk armed on established facts, preserves the evidence chain and un-attributed fault record for the Cabinet, continues supply coordination under County direction within existing budgeted authority, and issues no new claims, no standalone public statements, no official attribution, no engagement with Drevna's civilian offer, and takes no position on the inert verification or reinforcement options.
arguments.desired_effect: The crisis closes on the established-facts, civil-led record: essential services were sustained through restoration and handover and now transition to County-directed winter resilience under the joint framework; the standby desk and preserved evidence chain remain armed for any recurrence; CCA's civil protection stays coordinated with, but distinct from, the military's silent Cabinet-gated posture; no official attribution, no heightened alert, no standing foreign or Drevnian presence or corridor/no-go/notification regime, and no Drevna credit beyond the record; attribution, alert, verification renewal, foreign presence and any cooperation remain sole Cabinet decisions on evidence, with CCA opening no new public or decision fronts.
pros: The action creates no new claims, requests or public statements: it only executes already-committed civil tasks (winter-resilience pre-reads, armed standby desk, supply coordination), so the published close-out record stands unchanged and no new frictions open at the final turn.

It preserves the civil-led frame by completing the County-directed civilian transition while Defence Command's posture remains silent and Cabinet-gated, keeping civil protection and military activity coordinated but visibly distinct as the record and CCA's objectives require.

By holding the single joint County-CCA information channel and rebutting only with the established-facts record, it leaves the post-exercise 'government neglect' narrative no new CCA material to exploit and keeps public information accurate, timely and coordinated.

It protects attribution discipline and sensitive information: no attribution is made, tracing confidence, generator-stockpile size and dry-dock status remain undisclosed, and the evidence chain stays preserved for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority on evidence.

It reserves every decision right to the Cabinet - alert, attribution, foreign presence/consent, verification renewal and any Drevna civilian-channel engagement - and CCA takes no position on the inert verification or reinforcement options, consistent with all prior commitments.

arguments.action: Skarö County Administration formally stands up the County-directed winter-resilience programme on a civil-led footing: it confirms the early-October on-island working session with CCA at County offices (exact dates to be set after internal alignment with the municipality and the grid operator), begins review of CCA's four agenda pre-reads (island fuel reserve target, generator rotation and refresh, backup communications, drilled offload-and-sequencing), and keeps the joint County–CCA standby information desk armed to reactivate on established facts alone for any new disinformation surge or infrastructure event. Publication and reporting discipline is unchanged: jointly confirmed numbers only, Cabinet informed first on any event, no official attribution, and no statements beyond the published established-facts record (restoration sustained under County-directed recovery, cause unestablished, corridor unverified by either side, no standing presence).
arguments.desired_effect: Skarö's crisis response closes and converts to an operational, County-directed winter-resilience programme: essential-service resilience measures (island fuel reserve, generator rotation and refresh, backup communications, drilled offload-and-sequencing) are prepared for winter under the joint County–CCA framework, the standby joint information desk and the preserved un-attributed evidence chain remain armed for any recurrence, and the established-facts record stands as the sole public baseline without any new claim, escalation, standing foreign or Drevnian presence, corridor, no-go or notification regime, or ceded Cabinet decision right.
pros: Within County authority and the agreed County-CCA framework: no heightened alert, new mandate or Cabinet decision is needed to convert emergency logistics into routine winter-resilience measures on-island under County direction.

Concrete resilience deliverables follow from the restored grid and sustained fuel runway—fuel reserve target, generator rotation/refresh, backup comms and drilled offload-and-sequencing—turning crisis lessons into standing capacity that directly serves the County's core objective of keeping essential services running.

The armed standby desk, reacting on established facts alone with Cabinet-first reporting, means any future disinformation surge or infrastructure event is met with the civil-led factual baseline, keeping the public informed and calm without militarising the response or restating unverified claims.

Strictly consistent with the Cabinet's, CCA's, Defence Command's and Aldmoor's close-outs: no official attribution, no new claims, no standing foreign or Drevnian presence or regime, and attribution, alert, verification renewal and any cooperation left solely to the Cabinet on evidence.

Avoids friction at close-out and preserves the aligned civil-led recovery record as the concluding public baseline, denying the defeated 'neglect' and 'takeover' narratives any remaining factual predicate.

cons.reason: The decision establishes intentions, not the claimed outcomes. First, 'cable restoration deliverable in the following turn' is a contingency, not an effect: under the repair rule that outcome requires safe access to the fault to be secured in this same turn, and the Argument itself shows access depends on external deconfliction cooperation and on fault, seabed and sea-state conditions that no active fact establishes; any slippage extends Skarö's dependence on backup generation and seaborne fuel, so the core promised achievement is not delivered by this decision. Second, the claim that Drevna's long-announced exercise 'remains the visible anomaly' is a framing prediction the decision cannot guarantee: the novel visible fact this turn is a newly activated foreign military-supported repair operation at Skarö's landing site over an unattributed cause, and the open information environment records that any visible military activity at Skarö is framed as a takeover or militarisation whoever it serves — so the projected calm, unified civil-led public picture may be offset, not produced, by this activation, which also feeds the contested-attribution narratives the plan's own information pillar claims to counter.

The Desired Effect claims the crisis closes on Vardland-authored terms with the civil-led account standing as the concluding public record, but the Action's own premises preclude establishing that by this decision. The 48-hour validation outcome is not yet published when the decision is taken — the Action merely directs completion and publication within the window — so the transparency item is not closed by this decision, and no independent verification of the corridor or of Drevna's exercise conduct exists, as the decision itself candidly records. With the cause remaining unestablished under the published no-established-cause finding and public suspicion of the adjacent exercise persisting, the record after this decision still contains an unresolved cause, an unverified corridor and competing narratives; whether any single account stands as the concluding public record is therefore asserted rather than established on documented facts, so the claimed authoritative close may be limited in practice.

Drevna's claimed 'full clearance' is a unilateral self-declaration, not an independently verified fact: its exercise continues operating adjacent to the cable route and fuel corridor, and no third-party verification picture covers the corridor this window (Aldmoor's surveillance/overflight was not fully on station within its promised window, and the route stands without the transparency framework either side offered), so nothing independently establishes that safe access, the route and the fuel corridor are actually secured for repair and supply. The offered vessel records are conditioned on a Drevna-chosen 'scope' and format, and the desired effect pre-commits to 'no state attribution to Drevna' before the independent civilian examination's findings — prejudging that examination and the Cabinet's sole attribution authority. The effect therefore rests on unverifiable, self-selected assurances and cannot credibly deliver a verifiably incident-free, transparently documented window.

The package's core framing collapses against established facts: Vardland already has a civilian, County-led resupply chain under way — a fuel tanker about one day's sailing and mobile generators are being delivered through ordinary civilian/commercial channels coordinated by the Civil Contingencies Agency, with the County directing offloading — so Drevna's fuel offer is not the only civilian alternative, and declining it cannot be publicly framed as refusing civilian help or as proof of a slow, divided, politicised response. The 'de-escalatory' premise is likewise not established: a Drevnian repair vessel operating at the cable route and landing site while the cause remains unattributed and Drevna's own large exercise continues nearby could itself raise incident risk and public alarm, and the proposed no-go zones and pre-notification regimes would constrain the tanker, ferry and supply movements Skarö's residents depend on. The Desired Effect — establishing Drevna's response as civilian, transparent and de-escalatory and any Vardland non-acceptance as a public failure — therefore rests on premises contradicted by visible facts and would not survive scrutiny of the active situation.

Defence Command's Desired Effect asserts a close that the record does not yet support and a readiness that is not established. The 48-hour validation of Drevna's vessel-activity records is directed but not yet published, so the transparency item is not closed by this decision; and the Action's own premises concede the corridor was never independently verified by either side, so the claimed 'honest close-out record stands on preserved evidence' and a 'ready, evidence-based path to renew corridor verification' rest on a verification record that neither side produced during the window. Separately, the reinforcement-readiness figures (air ~1 day, sea ~2 days after a decision) are asserted rather than demonstrated: the established record documents that comparable promised timelines slipped in this crisis — the repair vessel's arrival and the maritime-surveillance stand-up were delayed beyond stated windows, and the overflight package was not fully on station within ~24 hours — so a fast, evidence-based response 'if unexplained activity recurs' is a posture claim, not a demonstrated capability. The Desired Effect's authoritative, de-escalated close with armed forces 'ready for recurrence' is therefore asserted, not established on documented facts, and may be limited in practice.

The Desired Effect's two central claims are not established by the action. First, the assurance that the reinforcement 'cannot be presented as a military takeover' and keeps the public frame civil-led is a framing prediction the decision cannot secure: the established open-information dynamic is that any visible military activity on or around Skarö is framed, whoever it serves, as takeover or militarisation, so an air- and sea-delivered deployment of national forces to the airfield, port and cable-landing site mid-crisis over an unattributed cause supplies the 'army takeover' and contested-attribution strands their most concrete material yet and becomes the salient visible event, offsetting rather than securing the civil-led picture the Desired Effect asserts. Second, the claimed survey outcome is not deliverable on the terms stated: a Defence Command-coordinated underwater survey is unilateral military evidence-gathering by one party in a contested-cause environment, not a transparent, agreed investigation, so any findings will be contested by actors not party to it and cannot by themselves establish cause for the very 'transparent' investigation Vardland has promised; no established fact shows the survey yields causality-determining evidence within the repair window, and conducting it at the fault site militarises the 'civilian' repair operation it is meant to protect, undercutting the operation's own legitimacy frame.

The desired effect claims protection outcomes and a public frame this action cannot establish, and its own terms defeat its central guarantee. (1) Protection is not secured by this action: the County transmits a request to the Cabinet — the decision it depends on is not part of this action, so 'the port, cable-landing site and airfield are protected through the window' is conditional on a political decision no active fact shows has been made; and the request does not close the legal blocker the effect says it removes, because the military-support-to-civil framework it invokes enumerates transport, engineering, surveillance and protection of military sites only, while the port, cable-landing site and airfield are civilian infrastructure — armed protection there would exceed that enumerated scope and require a Cabinet decision of real legal and political weight, not the 'single' settled authorisation the effect presents. The effect converts an open, contentious decision into an apparent settled outcome, while the island's actual protection remains whatever the Cabinet decides next turn. (2) The 'never presented as a military takeover' guarantee is undercut by the action's own request: it asks for visible armed elements at the three most visible sites over an unattributed cause and simultaneously claims the response will never be framed as a takeover — yet the information dynamic this very argument cites is that visible military activity on Skarö is framed as a takeover whoever it serves. A County-issued civil-led message before arrival is presentation, not control of the open information space; seeded accounts will amplify the imagery this request itself supplies at the moment of peak visibility, so the public-calm and civil-led components of the effect are materially at risk from the very presence requested.

The Desired Effect rests on a false dichotomy and on asymmetric compliance that will not hold. Vardland can accept civilian help in substance — commercial fuel and an independently crewed repair vessel under Vardland and County supervision with a neutral cause investigation — without joining Drevna's Safety-of-Navigation and Operations Protocol, so no 'stark choice' between a Drevnian civilian vessel and foreign military overflight actually exists. The Protocol also cuts both ways: its pre-notification, corridor and no-go terms would bind Aldmoor's and Vardland's movements while leaving Drevna's own large exercise near Skarö (which includes landing ships and continues in international waters) unconstrained and undisclosed, unless Drevna first shows it will constrain its exercise under the same rules. A protocol that exposes Vardland and Aldmoor while exempting the source of the tension is transparently one-sided and cannot establish Drevna as the responsible, de-escalatory party; its continuing exercise activity will dominate public framing and defeat the claimed effect.

The desired effect assumes acceptance would bind Aldmoor and refusal would prove Drevna's civilian framing, but both premises fail. First, the Protocol cannot bind Aldmoor: Aldmoor's participation depends on Aldmoor's own sovereign consent and on Vardland's Cabinet consent under host-nation rules, so Drevna cannot establish Aldmoor's limits by tabling a protocol and the claimed material reduction of Aldmoor's footprint is not achieved. Second, the stark binary is false: Vardland can and does take civilian help — commercial fuel and generator supply and its own contracted civilian repair — without accepting Drevna's political protocol; declining Drevna's package therefore does not demonstrate a militarised, slow or divided response. Third, the claimed de-escalatory, risk-reducing effect is limited: the no-go and pre-notification regime is symmetrical in text, yet Drevna files its own corridor plan while its large amphibious exercise near Skarö continues unconstrained, so incident risk around the repair site is not materially reduced unless Drevna itself constrains its exercise — which the package does not promise.

The Desired Effect's claim that residents receive a final bulletin that 'rebuts disinformation' is not deliverable on the established record. The bulletin is restricted to established facts, and the central fact the independent examination produced is that no cause of the failure was established - an indeterminate finding that documents Vardland's own failure to determine cause without excluding deliberate damage or foreign involvement; indeterminacy is not refutation, so the published record cannot by itself rebut the suspicion narratives, which is exactly why the cause remains the salient open question. It is already established this turn (50d76952) that the civil-frame documentation only partially offsets the militarisation/takeover framing, and the disinformation environment is driven by actors outside Vardland's control, so a single concluding publication cannot terminate it - particularly while the adjacent Drevnian exercise continues, the corridor remains unverified by either side, and no official attribution is made, leaving residents with a process document rather than closure on the cause. The Action can issue the bulletin and hand over coordination; it cannot establish that disinformation was rebutted, so that limb should be read as intent and documentation, not as a delivered effect.

The Desired Effect's guarantee that the reinforcement 'cannot be presented as a military takeover of the civilian response' is not established by this decision and is contradicted by the visible information environment. The open information monitor records that any visible military activity on Skarö is likely to be framed online as a 'takeover', whoever it serves, and the 'the army is preparing to take over Skarö' narrative is already live at medium reach and growing. An air-delivered element to the airfield and a sea-delivered element to the port during the repair and resupply window supplies fresh, concrete material for exactly that frame at the moment of peak visibility, while the joint public-information plan is working to keep the response demonstrably civil-led. An open Cabinet justification does not control the outcome: the frame is set by visible fact and the online environment, not by the announcement's wording. The civil-led public-frame component of the Desired Effect is therefore not achievable as claimed; unless the deployment is explicitly subordinated to and sequenced with the civilian information and supply plan, and the County's standing request for protection at these specific sites is confirmed, the visible reinforcement risks undercutting public trust in the civil-led response it claims to preserve.

The Desired Effect rests on two claims this authorisation cannot establish, and binding the Cabinet to them would undermine the credibility and lawfulness it must preserve. First, the effect asserts the reinforcement sits 'strictly' within the military-support-to-civil framework: that rule lets Defence Command support civil authorities only at a civil authority's request and only with transport, engineering, surveillance and protection of military sites. No established fact shows Skarö County has requested armed protection of the port, the airfield and the cable landing site — its standing request covers resupply and berthing priority — and the port and cable landing site are civilian infrastructure, not military sites within the rule's scope; an armed protection task there therefore exceeds the enumerated framework the effect cites as its lawful basis, so the claimed lawfulness is asserted, not established. Second, the effect guarantees the deployment 'cannot be presented as a military takeover of the civilian response': visible armed elements arriving on Skarö during an unattributed cable failure is precisely the trigger for the militarisation/takeover disinformation strands the Cabinet's own joint public-information plan is already countering, and Drevna has signalled it will frame any activation as militarisation; the Cabinet controls its own public line, not the open information environment, so that guarantee is undeliverable. The effect as written should be limited to what this authorisation can actually establish: a scoped, time-bound Cabinet decision whose legal basis and public framing are demonstrated rather than guaranteed.

Independent verification is not yet in place, so neither the claimed clearance nor any guarantee of 'no incident or interference' can be established at the point this effect is claimed: Aldmoor's surveillance/overflight is not fully on station within the promised window and a publicly visible gap remains in coverage of the cable route and fuel corridor. Drevna's offer of civilian vessel activity records is expressly conditional on an examination scope that has not been defined and remains voluntary, so it binds or verifies nothing during the repair window. The desired outcome therefore rests on Drevna's own unobserved, self-declared discipline exercised adjacent to the route, and on an attribution prerogative that belongs solely to the Vardland Cabinet, which this argument cannot pre-empt; a self-declared, unverified clearance cannot by itself produce the claimed effect.

The desired effect presumes facts the Cabinet has not yet established. The Aldmoor verification package was only activated this turn and is not confirmed as on station; through the whole crisis the corridor and Drevna's declared clear-hold have remained unverified by either side, so there is no verified incident-free record that an 'on-schedule, incident-free conclusion' and a 'natural lapse' of verification can rely on. Separately, Cabinet validation of Drevna's vessel records is pending, and the independent examination already published its no-established-cause finding before records arrived, so records 'showing no discrepancy' cannot be established now and cannot close the unresolved cause. If verification lapses 'naturally' on these unproven premises, the corridor returns to the unverified state at the crisis's start, leaving the cause unresolved, restoring Drevna's narrative initiative over its exercise and the deployment, and exposing the same unexplained activity to recur - so the claimed de-escalatory close is asserted, not achieved.

The Desired Effect's 'last word' limb is not deliverable by this Action on the established record. The fault-examination findings are published, but the cause of the cable failure remains unestablished - the published record can only document that no cause was determined, so it cannot close the fault question or remove the factual basis for suspicion narratives. The corridor likewise remains unverified: allied surveillance produced no confirmed incident-free or breach record, so the joint desk can publish that no verified record exists, not a verified account of the corridor; publishing established facts cannot convert an unverified space into a verified one. It is already established this turn that Drevna keeps the narrative initiative over the exercise and the visible deployment and that the civil-frame documentation only partially offsets the militarisation/takeover framing - a single civil-desk publication cannot by itself strip those narratives of their predicate. The Action can sequence the drawdown and issue documents; it cannot deliver the claimed last word on the fault or on how the deployment is publicly framed.

Drevna's framing is not within Vardland's control: the Desired Effect assures that 'Drevna gains no militarisation or takeover story,' but that is an asserted outcome over another actor's public narrative, not something this Action can deliver or verify. Drevna has already publicly characterised Vardland's handling of the outage as provocative militarisation, and the Cabinet's authorisation of a visible, armed air-and-sea protection element on the island — regardless of advance announcement, civil-led sequencing, or time-bound scope — supplies exactly the image on which that characterisation builds, in a setting where the cable's cause is still unresolved and the Drevnian exercise is already the salient visible anomaly. The Action can secure the sequencing and messaging of its own deployment; it cannot foreclose how Drevna, its media environment, or third parties present that deployment, still less convert the absence of armed escalation into the absence of a narrative. Crediting this limb would treat intent as outcome: what is established at most is that Vardland intends a civil frame, not that Drevna gains no story. That limb should be limited to intent, and the effect's central claim — that the deployment can be made politically cost-free by framing alone — is not produced by this Action.

Crediting the Desired Effect would preempt the investigation: the 'no state attribution of the cable failure to Drevna' limb presumes a conclusion the Action cannot deliver. The independent civilian examination's scope is still undefined, the records Drevna promises are conditional and self-selected, and under Vardland rules only the Cabinet can attribute on evidence - so that limb is a political claim, not an outcome this Action achieves. The clearance premise is likewise unverified: the clearance is self-declared, and the independent surveillance Drevna's own pros invoke as verification was not on station within the promised window last turn and is not yet confirmed holding, so 'no incident or interference' rests on Drevna's assertion rather than established fact.

The package's civilian and de-escalatory framing fails on its own design: the Safety-of-Navigation and Operations Protocol is authored by the state that, by its own announcement, is simultaneously running a large naval and air exercise in the waters off Skarö. Drevna would submit the corridor plan immediately and receive pre-notification of all military and civilian movements around Vardland's cable route, landing site and repair operations, while Drevna itself defines the no-go zones. This is not neutral safety coordination: it hands the most interested party the authority to set operational rules around Vardland's own critical infrastructure, to track every resupply movement and to constrain allied overflight and surveillance of its exercise — increasing, not reducing, the risk of an incident or of justified distrust. Pre-notification of all civilian movements also adds procedural friction to the fuel and generator resupply on which Skarö's hospitals, water and heating depend, the binding constraint of the crisis. The 'stark choice' framing is a false binary: accepting civilian aid need not mean accepting Drevna's rule-setting, since Vardland is already running a civilian-led response with its own means and ordinary commercial channels and can accept assistance on its own terms. The desired effect — a transparent, de-escalatory civilian arrangement that locks down Aldmoor's footprint — is therefore not what the package delivers: acceptance would cede agenda- and rule-setting around Vardland infrastructure to an adversary mid-exercise, and it would equally be Vardland, not Drevna, who is seen to have chosen.

The Desired Effect's central claim — that surging surveillance now closes the corridor visibility gap and that 'the corridor no longer stands as unverified by either side' — is not deliverable on the established record, and crediting it would undermine the civil-led record the CCA and County just published through the joint desk. The consent/restoration window has already concluded: the cable was restored in the extended window, the independent civilian examination completed and published its findings, the time-bound armed protection drew down on schedule, and Skarö County has formally closed out the emergency response, with the final joint bulletin documenting the corridor as unverified by either side. Surveillance stood up now is forward-looking; it cannot retroactively close a gap that existed during the window or convert the already-published 'unverified' record into a verified one. If the surged picture instead finds no excursion, it would independently validate exactly the Drevna clear-hold claim the close-out deliberately left unverified — handing Drevna narrative credit for a corridor whose operational purpose (repair access, fuel supply) has already ended. Delivering fault records and an un-attributed maritime picture 'before any disturbance' is likewise moot: the examination has concluded and its findings are published. And the renewable verification option, tied to 'as long as the exercise continues,' would, if accepted, re-open a continuing foreign surveillance presence over Skarö during the recovery phase — the lingering foreign footprint the civil-led close-out committed to avoiding — under a fresh host-nation-consent decision that has not been made. The Action can report the earlier gap candidly and complete its stand-down; it cannot deliver a verified-corridor outcome the record has already closed without falsifying the accurate civil-led record.

Drevna's clearance is unilateral self-certification, not an established fact of safe access: it asserts its own exercise's discipline over a fault working area and a corridor under Vardland jurisdiction, while the allied surveillance Drevna cites for verification was not fully on station within the first 24-hour window, leaving an unobserved period in exactly those waters. The effect's guarantees - safe access intact, no incident or interference, no attribution - can only hold if confirmed by Vardland-side observation and the independent civilian examination, not by the exercising state's own assurance. That is especially true since Drevna's promised participation is conditional on an examination scope 'once defined' that Drevna can postpone, withholding the very records on which the no-attribution conclusion would depend. Any exercise-related vessel presence or interference documented during the unobserved period would defeat the effect.

This Argument's core premise — that full execution stays within the already-consented scope and needs no new authority — fails for two elements it asserts as execution. (1) Overflight: the Cabinet's established consent covers the scoped cable-repair operation with limited supporting maritime surveillance and Defence Command backing; no Cabinet decision allows Aldmoor surveillance aircraft into Vardland airspace, and foreign military aircraft may operate there only on a Cabinet decision under host-nation consent — so 'overflight on station within ~24 hours' over the cable route and fuel-resupply corridor is not established by Aldmoor's own action. (2) Survey: facilitating a Defence Command-coordinated underwater survey presumes an expanded military evidence role no active fact authorises — the Cabinet deliberately kept that decision open for the transparent cause investigation — so the Desired Effect's assertion of 'no expansion beyond the consented areas' is not deliverable by this action alone. The consented repair vessel and maritime-surveillance core can proceed, but the overflight and survey elements require the Cabinet's own decisions, not allied execution of them.

Drevna's desired effect presupposes facts not established on the record. It asserts its vessel-activity records were delivered 'in full' and show 'no discrepancy,' yet completion against Vardland's defined scope, format and timetable is still subject to the ongoing technical inspection, whose outcome is to be published on established facts at the 48-hour validation deadline — valid, or unfilled. Its claim of an incident-free, on-schedule conclusion is likewise self-reported: established facts record that neither side produced an acknowledged verification record of the corridor during the exercise window, so no documented record yet supports a clean lapse of verification, 'no factual predicate' for renewal, or a closed file. The de-escalatory close therefore rests on unverified assertions rather than established facts and cannot foreclose the Cabinet's sole renewal decision or record Drevna's transparency as showing no discrepancy.

Two components of the Desired Effect cannot be established by this action. First, the protection gap is not 'removed in law and framing': only the Vardland Cabinet can authorise armed force on Vardland territory and no Cabinet authorisation exists here — formalising a County request prepares a decision, it does not close the gap; and the military-support-to-civil framework the request invokes limits Defence Command support to transport, engineering, surveillance and protection of military sites, while the port, cable-landing site and airfield are civilian infrastructure, so the asserted 'civil-authority basis' cannot cure that framework limit and the blocker persists until an actual Cabinet decision. Second, the sequencing and framing guarantees are not CCA's to make: it neither directs Defence Command deployments nor controls the open information space, so it cannot commit that any visible armed presence will be 'sequenced behind' the civilian plan or 'never presented as a military takeover'; the established dynamic is that visible armed elements on Skarö over an unattributed cause are framed as takeover whoever they serve, so the civil-led public frame is at risk, not secured. 'Restoration deliverable next turn' likewise remains contingent on safe access holding through the window, which logistics coordination alone does not guarantee.

The Desired Effect treats two things as established that Drevna's action cannot establish. The published close-out record states the repair-window corridor was never independently verified by either side and Drevna's declared clear-hold remains unverified, so an 'incident-free' conclusion cannot be certified as fact or grant Drevna corridor-safety credit. Likewise, the vessel-activity records item remains pending the Cabinet's 48-hour validation against Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable; unless and until the Cabinet confirms full compliance, it is an unfilled transparency commitment, not evidence of 'no discrepancy.' Drevna cannot unilaterally convert its claimed delivery into a validated record or into a lapse 'with no predicate' - the validation finding and any lapse or renewal rest with the Cabinet on the evidence, not with Drevna's framing.

The claimed effect that Drevna 'preserves its credibility and a functioning civilian channel' is not supported by the established record and cannot be established by this action: the published record fixes that the corridor was unverified by either side through the window, that Drevna's self-reported clear-hold and no-incident conclusion gained no Vardland validation or safety credit, and that the cable's cause remains unestablished. A silent, internal close-out plus an offer to confirm only 'if Vardland initiates' supplies no independent confirmation and no conceded record; any civilian channel remains available solely on Vardland-defined terms and a fresh Cabinet decision, neither of which this action creates. 'Credibility' resting on Drevna's own unverified account is a political claim, not an established fact, so the effect is limited to the parts the record already grants (no attribution by any side, no standing presence, Cabinet's retained authority) and Drevna leaves the crisis without an adjudicated clean-exit credit.

The guarantees at the heart of this Argument are not independently verifiable as stated: Aldmoor's maritime surveillance and overflight were already not fully on station within their promised window last turn, leaving a visibility gap over exactly the cable route and fuel corridor now claimed 'cleared,' while the clearance is a boundary Drevna itself draws and polices beside an exercise that continues unconstrained in the same waters — so an excursion or interference at or inside that self-declared boundary could go undetected, leaving the 'no incident or interference' outcome unestablished, and the promised vessel-activity records are conditional on an examination 'scope' that Drevna alone can define or delay, meaning the civilian examination could conclude with the fault only partially documented.

The Desired Effect's linchpin — that the corridor 'no longer stands as unverified by either side' — rests on a within-24h on-station claim the established record already contradicts: the same surveillance/overflight package was not fully on station within its promised ~24-hour window last turn (53f70cec), its stand-up slipped and coordination was incomplete (46838ce4, 67b87351), and the allied picture never closed the corridor gap (fbd6888f). The Action repeats the identical within-24h surge commitment while in the same breath candidly reporting the earlier gap — acknowledging the shortfall without establishing any mechanism that remedies it — so the corridor's status change is asserted at the point of action rather than delivered; on the established record the corridor can remain unverified by either side exactly as before. Even if assets do reach station, the 'complete' un-attributed maritime picture this Action promises to deliver is the same picture established to contain stand-up gaps, so neither the claimed complete evidence chain nor the 'verification alternative visibly functions' outcome is producible by this Action on this record.

Aldmoor's own operational friction is established fact: the repair vessel's arrival or the maritime-surveillance stand-up was already delayed beyond the stated windows, and Skarö County itself states restoration is taking longer than projected. On top of that already-slipped schedule the Cabinet inserts a further 48-hour examination gate before any disturbance of the fault and before restoration begins, within a roughly five-day fuel runway. The Desired Effect claims the restoration window completes with the cable restored and Skarö's fuel-by-sea dependence ended, but this decision establishes no mechanism by which the added examination gate is absorbed into the timeline; on the established timescales it extends, not ends, the island's reliance on fuel by sea or air and pushes restoration past the window, so the effect's central outcome is not delivered by this action.

The Desired Effect's guarantee that the reinforcement 'cannot be presented as a military takeover of the civilian response' cannot be established by this action and is contradicted by the active information environment the County monitors on Skarö. Visible effects already record the 'government caused the outage through neglect' narrative spreading quickly, and the County's on-island monitoring records an active, growing 'army preparing to take over Skarö' narrative propagated through newly created accounts, with the working assessment that any visible military activity on Skarö is framed as a takeover regardless of its legal framing. An air-delivered element arriving at the airfield and cable-landing area within about a day and a sea-delivered element within two days is the most visible footprint available — uniformed personnel at the three sites residents can see — arriving at the moment of peak anxiety, in practice replacing civilian responders as the face of the crisis and supplying exactly the imagery those seeded narratives and Drevna's parallel 'militarisation of the response' line need. A Cabinet public frame cannot control a contested, adversarially seeded information space: an announcement that troops are deployed to 'protect the cable' can confirm the takeover story as readily as blunt it. Because the public outcome at the heart of the effect rests on a framing prediction this action cannot deliver, the claimed civil-led, calm-public result is not established by the action; at minimum the effect is materially limited, and the deployment risks the very loss of public confidence it claims to prevent.

The claimed civilian/transparent/de-escalatory effect is not established by this package: the proposed protocol binds only movements that states choose to file, while Drevna's own large naval and air exercise near Skarö continues outside the protocol's scope—unreported and unconstrained under it—so the largest military presence in the area escapes the very transparency and incident-risk guarantees the package claims. The 'stark choice' framing likewise fails: Vardland can accept civilian fuel, generators or even repair help through ordinary, County-led channels under its own authority without endorsing Drevna's standing, so declining or routing this offer does not by itself expose a slow or divided Vardland response; and the offer's civilian character is undercut by the offerer's concurrent exercise in the same waters.

The survey component is not within the consented scope and defeats the Desired Effect's own containment claim. The active consent record is explicit: no Defence Command-coordinated underwater survey of the fault is authorised, and the Aldmoor operation continues under the already-scoped consent without an expanded military evidence role. This action nevertheless claims to facilitate a Defence Command-coordinated underwater survey 'within the consented scope' — an authorisation that no active fact establishes and that Aldmoor cannot create. Either branch defeats the effect: if the survey is not authorised, the claimed executed-in-full, credible role is not delivered and the survey component of the Desired Effect fails; if Aldmoor's facilitation in practice scripts Defence Command to collect at the fault, that is precisely the expanded military evidence role the consent record excludes — an expansion, not containment — and unilateral military collection at a contested site before the transparent investigation's modalities are agreed leaves cause determination to one party's military arm rather than to the transparent investigation and the Vardland Cabinet, as the Desired Effect claims. The Desired Effect's core assertions — full execution, no expansion beyond the consented areas, and a credible civil-led, investigation-respecting operation — are therefore not established by this action.

Drevna's desired effect presumes its own self-assessment closes the record ('completed records transparency showing no discrepancy'; an incident-free conclusion validates its clearance discipline), but the established record contradicts this: the published record shows Drevna's vessel-activity records obligation was still a live, unfilled transparency item timed after the independent examination had already published its no-established-cause finding, the Cabinet has not confirmed receipt as of this turn, no civilian validation has occurred, and both Vardland and Aldmoor continue to treat the corridor as unverified by either side. A self-reported clean record and clean conduct is not evidence under the qualitative-posture rule, so the effect cannot independently certify 'no discrepancy' or make continued Cabinet-authorised verification look divorced from facts; and the claimed 'natural lapse' of corridor verification presumes a Cabinet renewal decision that only the Cabinet can make and that remains pending.

The effect's core premise - an incident-free, on-schedule conclusion and records transparency 'showing no discrepancy' - is not established fact. The corridor has been unverified by either side throughout: Aldmoor's earlier surveillance did not close the visibility gap, and Drevna's self-declared clearance boundary was never independently confirmed, so Drevna's 'no incident' conduct is an absence-of-observation assertion, not a verified record. Likewise, whether the delivered vessel-activity records contain discrepancies is precisely what the Cabinet's pending validation is to determine; until that validation is published, Drevna cannot claim the transparency item is complete 'with no discrepancy.' The desired effect seeks to convert an unverified corridor and an unfinished validation into an acknowledged clean close, which the existing adjudicated record does not support.

Drevna's desired effect overstates the record on the two items it asks to carry forward: 'preserved credibility' and 'a functioning civilian channel for any future good-neighbourly cooperation.' The adjudicated turn-3 record holds that Drevna's exercise-conclusion conduct is self-reported and unverified by either side, that its corridor clear-hold received no Vardland validation and gains no safety credit, and that its vessel-activity records were validated only on Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable, closing as 'valid or unfilled' with the Cabinet-directed record expressly declining to treat Drevna's 'no discrepancy' framing as an established finding. No civilian cooperation mechanism was ever established in fact: the Drevnian Protocol was formally declined in turn 1, the repair and cooperation offer was never accepted, scoped or activated by the Cabinet, and the only live civilian channel was the Vardland-defined records validation, which has now closed. An effect that awards Drevna residual credibility and a functioning cooperation channel therefore exceeds the established facts, and by gifting unearned credit at the moment of close-out it would reintroduce precisely the narrative residue Drevna's restraint claims to avoid, undercutting the Cabinet-reserved conclusion that attribution, verification and any cooperation decisions rest solely on the Cabinet on evidence.

effects.description: For the remainder of the repair window, the Skarö cable route and fuel-resupply corridor is now without the transparency framework that either side offered this turn: Vardland declined Drevna's Safety-of-Navigation and Operations Protocol as tabled, and Aldmoor's maritime surveillance and overflight are not fully on station within the promised window. The Drevnian exercise therefore continues in the area unconstrained, and no corridor pre-notification or full allied observation picture covers the route.
effects.rationale: The Cabinet's formal decline of the Drevnian protocol, the failure of Aldmoor's surveillance stand-up, and the continuing unconstrained Drevnian exercise only produce this observation and pre-notification gap when read together. No single adjudication created it.

effects.description: The armed-protection question for Skarö has converged into one unresolved Cabinet decision point: Skarö County's formal scoped armed-protection request and Defence Command's scoped reinforcement request are both pending before the Cabinet and cover the same sites and restoration window, but no Cabinet authorisation has been issued. No armed element moves this turn, and the port, cable-landing site and airfield remain without the requested protection while the civilian response and Aldmoor repair operation continue.
effects.rationale: Defence Command's request is formally pending without authorisation, while CCA and Skarö County have formalised a matching civil-authority request. Under `military-support-to-civil` and `host-nation-consent`, the Cabinet is the only body that can release the requested armed element, so the convergence of these two requests makes it the sole remaining decision point for the protection gap.

effects.description: Skarö's repair path is now tied to the delayed Aldmoor operation: the Cabinet has not requested the Drevnian civilian repair vessel involved in the Drevna package, and Aldmoor's operational friction pushes cable restoration later than projected. Skarö therefore remains on backup generation and dependent on fuel by sea or air for a longer period than the repair-window plan counted on.
effects.rationale: The Cabinet's decision ruled out the Drevnian civilian repair vessel while keeping ordinary resupply, and Aldmoor's failure establishes a delay beyond the stated windows. Under `cable-repair-time`, the delayed vessel directly extends Skarö's reliance on backup generation and fuel deliveries, a combined consequence neither the decline nor the delay produces alone.

effects.description: Skarö's response closes with no active independent verification over the cable route or fuel corridor: the County has transitioned to routine recovery, Aldmoor's surveillance has stood down, and the Drevnian exercise continues adjacent to Skarö. Aldmoor's renewable, time-bound verification option is the only pending mechanism that could restore visibility, and it awaits a fresh Cabinet decision.
effects.rationale: The formal close-out of emergency coordination and Aldmoor's completed stand-down with no standing presence combine with the unclosed surveillance gap and the continuing, documented Drevnian exercise to leave an end-of-turn state in which the corridor is unmonitored while the exercise continues.

effects.description: Drevna's civilian vessel activity records commitment remains a live but unfilled transparency item after the independent examination has already published its no-established-cause finding; the records obligation is now timed after the finding rather than as an input to it.
effects.rationale: The Cabinet defined the scope, format and timetable and thereby activated Drevna's conditional records commitment, and Drevna confirmed it would provide the records once that scope was defined. The examination's no-established-cause finding was already published through the joint County–CCA desk, so the interaction leaves the records obligation timed after the finding rather than feeding into it.

effects.description: With the Drevnian exercise concluded and its forces departed, no visible foreign explanation for the cable failure remains in public view, while the published close-out record leaves the cause unestablished and the corridor unverified by either side. The previously active online claim that Vardland government neglect caused the outage therefore no longer faces a salient competing explanation, and rebuttal of it rests solely on the armed joint County–CCA standby desk responding with the established-facts record.
effects.rationale: Drevna's incident-free, on-schedule exercise conclusion removes the foreign exercise that had been the most visible alternative context, and the Cabinet's candid record confirms no official attribution and an unestablished cause. Combining the still-active government-neglect narrative with that confirmed absence of any attributed cause means the neglect claim is now the only explanation in circulation that a reader can infer, making the standby desk's established-facts-only rebuttal the decisive counterweight. This follows from Drevna's close-out and the Cabinet's record taken together, not from any single adjudication.

effects.description: Vardland now holds a coherent, fully Cabinet-gated recurrence-response posture assembled from separate close-outs: a preserved evidence chain and un-attributed fault record for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority, an armed standby joint information desk reactivating on established facts alone, a private internal Skarö garrison readiness, and renewable time-bound options for corridor verification and air/sea reinforcement, each requiring a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence. Any future disturbance of the cable restarts this standing sequence without any standing foreign or military presence.
effects.rationale: No single actor created this capability on its own: Defence Command preserved the evidence and held the reinforcement and verification options, the CCA and Skarö County armed the standby information-desk protocol, and Aldmoor left the verification option renewable only on a fresh Cabinet decision while withdrawing completely. Taken together these close-outs aggregate into an integrated readiness posture in which attribution, verification renewal and reinforcement are all Cabinet decisions and no standing allied or Drevnian mechanism survives.
