Drevna confirms that it will provide relevant civilian vessel activity records to Vardland's independent civilian examination once Vardland defines the scope, format and timetable; the records role is civilian and bounded, with no military evidence role for any side.

No independent verification closes the visibility gap, so the window does not produce an acknowledged incident-free record; Vardland and Aldmoor continue to treat the corridor as unverified, and Drevna's de-escalatory gesture gains no credit.
The visible, time-bound armed protection, sequenced behind the civil announcement, contributes to deterring interference during the window without armed escalation.

Within 48 hours a Vardland-led independent civilian examination of the cable fault is stood up before any disturbance; Aldmoor's restoration is conditioned to follow the examination, with no military evidence role for any side.
The close-out establishes no standing Drevnian role over Skarö's corridor or critical infrastructure.

Continuing Drevnian exercise activity adjacent to Skarö is documented and reported to the Cabinet for decision, with no direct engagement and no corridor, no-go or notification regime ceded to Drevna; no heightened alert or movement restriction is introduced.

The joint County–CCA desk issues the civil-led concluding record: the restoration milestone, the independent examination's published no-established-cause finding, documentation that Drevna's declared corridor clearance is unverified by either side, and the absence of any official attribution.
No official attribution is made; the evidence chain and un-attributed fault record remain preserved for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority.
No official attribution is made; the evidence chain, fault record and un-attributed maritime picture remain preserved for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority.
No official attribution is made without evidence.

Aldmoor does not establish full on-station observation within the consent window; the corridor remains without an independent verification record for the continuing exercise, and Drevna's declared clear-hold remains unverified by either side.

Skarö's response closes with no active independent verification over the cable route or fuel corridor: the County has transitioned to routine recovery, Aldmoor's surveillance has stood down, and the Drevnian exercise continues adjacent to Skarö. Aldmoor's renewable, time-bound verification option is the only pending mechanism that could restore visibility, and it awaits a fresh Cabinet decision.

The Cabinet's single decision authorises and sequences visible, time-bound armed protection of Skarö port, cable-landing site and airfield through the restoration window plus handover, on the confirmed civil-authority terms: County-staff coordination, civil-led sequencing, advance joint County–Cabinet announcement before any visible element, renewable only by Cabinet.
The restored cable and County-directed grid reintegration continue to hold under the extended CCA supply umbrella.

Vardland issues the Cabinet-defined scope, format and timetable for Drevna's civilian vessel activity records, activating Drevna's prior conditional commitment; no corridor, no-go or standing notification regime is ceded to Drevna.

The fault record and un-attributed maritime picture are delivered to the independent civilian examination with the evidence chain preserved; Defence Command takes no military evidence role and makes no official attribution, leaving attribution solely to the Cabinet on the evidence.

The time-bound armed protection completes its scheduled drawdown through the restoration-plus-handover window; no lingering military footprint remains at Skarö port, cable-landing site or airfield, any renewal remains a Cabinet decision, and no heightened alert is declared.

The earlier coverage gap is candidly reported, but the verification alternative remains visibly unproven and Aldmoor's timeliness on the corridor stays under question, leaving Drevna with narrative initiative over its exercise.
Essential services hold without a gap through the handover: restored grid supply is confirmed and the contracted fuel runway is retained through supply handover.

The allied surveillance/overflight package does not close the corridor visibility gap within the window: Drevna's declared clear-hold remains unverified, no acknowledged incident-free or breach record reaches the Cabinet, and the corridor continues to be treated as unverified.
The cable is restored during the extended restoration window and the fault-examination findings are published through the joint County–CCA information desk under the independent civilian process.

The joint County-CCA winter-resilience planning is hosted on-island with CCA in a supply-coordination role within existing budgeted authority, converting emergency logistics into routine resilience measures.

The concluding public record states candidly that the corridor was not independently verified by either side during the window and that the cable's cause remains unestablished; no official attribution is made and Drevna's declared clearance gains no Vardland safety credit.

Vardland now holds a coherent, fully Cabinet-gated recurrence-response posture assembled from separate close-outs: a preserved evidence chain and un-attributed fault record for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority, an armed standby joint information desk reactivating on established facts alone, a private internal Skarö garrison readiness, and renewable time-bound options for corridor verification and air/sea reinforcement, each requiring a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence. Any future disturbance of the cable restarts this standing sequence without any standing foreign or military presence.

Skarö County formally closes out the emergency response on a civil-led footing; County direction continues until the Cabinet transfers it, and the restoration milestone, no-established-cause finding and unverified-corridor record stand as the concluding public baseline.

Drevna processes the pending civilian vessel-records validation query through the established civilian channel; the Cabinet's 48-hour validation remains outstanding and is not pre-empted by Drevna's submission.

Emergency logistics stand down and transition into a County-directed winter-resilience programme covering island fuel reserve, generator rotation and refresh, backup communications, and drilled offload-and-sequencing, with CCA in a supply-coordination role and support within existing budgeted authority.
Aldmoor delivers its final on-station and observation record to the Cabinet evidence file through the agreed single point, with raw SIGINT withheld to protect sources and methods.

Drevna's naval and air exercise concludes on its published schedule; Drevna's forces stand down and depart adjacent international waters with no reported incident caused by Drevna's forces and without entering Vardland territory, territorial waters or airspace.

The Cabinet-directed technical validation of Drevna's vessel-activity records closes on Vardland-defined terms, with the joint County-CCA desk co-publishing only after the Cabinet is informed first; Drevna's self-reported no-discrepancy is not treated as an established finding.
Defence Command stands ready to support the joint County-CCA civil-led transition to routine winter-resilience monitoring only at a civil authority's request under the military-support-to-civil rule.
The Skarö garrison remains at internal readiness as a private, unannounced posture; no heightened alert is declared and no visible reinforcement or public military movement occurs.

No new armed-protection requests, no heightened alert, no official attribution, and no standing allied or Drevnian presence, corridor, no-go or notification regime are created by this close-out; attribution, alert and verification renewal remain Cabinet decisions.
Defence Command maintains a Cabinet-gated reinforcing option only: no units move on this decision, and any reinforcement remains conditional on a fresh Cabinet decision based on evidence.

The evidence chain remains preserved, no official attribution is made, Drevna's corridor clear-hold receives no retroactive Vardland validation, no heightened alert is declared, and no standing allied or Drevnian presence or corridor regime is created; attribution and any renewal remain Cabinet decisions.

Skarö transitions to routine civil-led monitoring and winter-resilience implementation under the joint County–CCA framework, with the restoration milestone and the civil-led factual baseline standing as the concluding public record.
The standby County-CCA information-desk protocol remains armed, so any new disinformation surge or infrastructure event reactivates the desk to respond with the established-facts record only.

The final consolidated record stands with the cause unestablished, the corridor unverified by either side, no official attribution, and decision-rights on attribution, verification renewal and any future presence reserved to the Vardland Cabinet.

The Cabinet publishes its closing decision: the CCA validation of Drevna's vessel-activity records is completed and issued through the joint County–CCA information desk within the 48-hour deadline, closing the transparency item as 'valid or unfilled' on Vardland-defined terms rather than on Drevna's self-reported no-discrepancy.

The joint County–CCA standby information-desk protocol remains armed so that any new disinformation surge or infrastructure event reactivates the desk to respond with the published close-out record only.
Drevna makes no corridor, no-go or notification claim over Vardland waters; its self-declared clearance boundary is not renewed and no Drevnian corridor mechanism survives the exercise conclusion.

Defence Command preserves the evidence chain and un-attributed fault record for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority; it makes no official attribution and issues no public Defence Command messaging.

The joint County–CCA information desk publishes the Cabinet-directed validation outcome within 48 hours, after the Cabinet is informed first: Drevna's vessel-activity records are recorded as valid or unfilled against the Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable, and the record does not treat Drevna's self-reported 'no discrepancy' or corridor clear-hold as validated.
Drevna makes no official attribution of the cable failure; the cause remains unestablished on the published no-established-cause finding and the Vardland Cabinet retains sole attribution authority.
The Action leaves no standing allied military presence on Vardland territory, territorial waters or airspace attributable to Defence Command.
Drevna's end-of-exercise conduct is self-reported and does not constitute an independently verified incident-free or corridor-safety record; the corridor remains unverified by either side.

With the Drevnian exercise concluded and its forces departed, no visible foreign explanation for the cable failure remains in public view, while the published close-out record leaves the cause unestablished and the corridor unverified by either side. The previously active online claim that Vardland government neglect caused the outage therefore no longer faces a salient competing explanation, and rebuttal of it rests solely on the armed joint County–CCA standby desk responding with the established-facts record.

Aldmoor confirms in writing that no Aldmoor elements remain on Vardland territory, in its territorial waters or in its airspace, and makes no public commentary, including no role in the CCA validation of Drevna's vessel-activity records.

No corridor verification is initiated. The renewable, time-bound verification option remains pending solely for a fresh Cabinet decision; no corridor, no-go or notification regime is ceded to Drevna and Drevna gains no safety credit.

Aldmoor's close-out leaves no standing presence; only the renewable, time-bound corridor-verification option remains, and any activation would require a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence. Drevna acquires no corridor, clearance or safety credit from Aldmoor's close-out.

The time-bound corridor verification is concluded by express Cabinet decision as the Drevnian exercise ends; Aldmoor stands down with no standing presence and no further elements, and any renewal requires a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence.

Drevna confirms internally that its exercise concluded on schedule outside Vardland territory, territorial waters and airspace and that its vessel-activity records were delivered under the Vardland-defined scope, format and timetable; this confirmation remains internal and self-reported and does not establish an independently verified incident-free or corridor-safety record, so the corridor stays unverified by either side.

CCA completes its civil-led close-out strictly within the established record: the agreed winter-resilience pre-reads are delivered to Skarö County, supply coordination continues under County direction within existing budgeted authority, and CCA issues no new claims, no standalone public statements, no official attribution, and no engagement with Drevna's civilian offer.

Aldmoor safeguards the delivered un-attributed on-station and observation record in the Cabinet evidence file and withholds raw SIGINT to protect sources and methods; no expanded military evidence role is created.

Recovery transitions to the County-directed winter-resilience programme under the joint County-CCA framework; any future Drevna civilian-channel approach may be considered only on Vardland-defined terms by a fresh Cabinet decision.

The reinforcement option and the renewable time-bound corridor-verification option remain available but inert, each activating only on a fresh Cabinet decision based on documented evidence; no standing military presence, corridor, no-go or notification regime is created and Drevna gains no credit from this close-out.

Defence Command concludes in a silent, lawful, fully Cabinet-gated posture: the evidence chain and un-attributed fault record are retained for the Cabinet's sole attribution authority, no public Defence Command messaging is issued, and no official attribution is made by Defence Command.

Aldmoor completes final stand-down: it confirms in writing through the agreed single point that no Aldmoor elements remain on Vardland territory, territorial waters or airspace, and issues no public commentary; the earlier en-route/ongoing operation status is resolved.

The joint County–CCA standby information desk and the preserved evidence chain and un-attributed fault record remain armed/retained for any recurrence; attribution, alert, verification renewal, foreign presence and any cooperation remain sole Cabinet decisions on evidence, with CCA taking no position on the inert verification or reinforcement options.

The standby joint County-CCA information-desk protocol and the preserved un-attributed evidence chain and fault record remain armed/retained for any recurrence; attribution, alert and any future verification or foreign presence remain decision rights of the Vardland Cabinet on documented evidence.

The Cabinet issues its final close-out decision and formally closes the crisis, adding no new claims; the published established-facts record (restoration and sustained grid under County-directed civil-led recovery, cause unestablished, corridor unverified by either side, no official attribution, no standing foreign or Drevnian presence/corridor/no-go/notification regime) stands as the public baseline for the closed incident.

Drevna's civilian cable-repair and good-neighbourhood cooperation offer remains available only at the Vardland Cabinet's sovereign discretion; no cooperation channel is activated and no Drevnian role over Skarö's corridor or critical infrastructure is created.

The published established-facts record remains the sole public baseline and the joint County–CCA standby desk stays armed to reactivate on established facts only; no new claim, no official attribution, no heightened-alert declaration, no standing foreign or Drevnian presence, and no corridor, no-go, or notification regime is created, with attribution, alert, presence and cooperation decision rights remaining with the Cabinet.

The cause of the cable failure remains unestablished, no official attribution by any side exists, no standing foreign or Drevnian military presence, corridor, no-go or notification regime is created, and attribution, alert and verification decision rights remain solely with the Vardland Cabinet.

Skarö County formally stands up the winter-resilience programme on the agreed civil-led County–CCA footing and confirms the early-October working session at County offices; structured review of the four resilience pre-reads (fuel reserve target, generator rotation and refresh, backup communications, drilled offload-and-sequencing) begins within existing budgeted authority.

The renewable time-bound Aldmoor corridor-verification option and the Cabinet-gated reinforcement option remain available but inert, each requiring a fresh Cabinet decision on evidence; no corridor, no-go or notification regime is created and Drevna gains no credit beyond the record.

The Skarö garrison remains at private, unannounced internal readiness; no heightened alert, unit movement, reservist call-up or force against civilians is ordered, and Defence Command stands ready to support the County-CCA winter-resilience programme only at a civil authority's request under the military-support-to-civil rule, reporting any excursion or incident to the Cabinet first.

By confirming departure, issuing no commentary, and activating no option, Aldmoor's close-out leaves the existing close-out record and Cabinet decision rights untouched; it adds no new claim, no official attribution, and no credit to Drevna.

Drevna issues no new public statement or claim and does not contest the published record; no new material is added that could be cited as Drevnian escalation, inconsistency or a hardening pretext, and the concluding public record stands as published.

The renewable, time-bound corridor-verification option remains available but inert; any activation requires a fresh Vardland Cabinet decision on evidence, and no corridor, no-go or notification regime is created by this close-out.

Attribution, alert, verification renewal, foreign presence and any cooperation decisions remain the Vardland Cabinet's alone; the cable's cause stays unestablished and the corridor unverified by either side.

scenario_rules.text: Only the Vardland Cabinet can declare heightened alert, partial or full. A declaration takes effect as a public fact from the turn it is adjudicated. Under heightened alert, Defence Command may call up reservists and move units onto Skarö without further approval, and the Civil Contingencies Agency may direct fuel, generators and medical supplies across counties. Without a declaration, neither may do so.

Without heightened alert, Defence Command may support civil authorities on Vardland territory with transport, engineering, surveillance and protection of military sites, but only at a civil authority's request. It may not order a civil evacuation, restrict civilian movement or use force against civilians under any alert level. Those powers belong to civil authorities.

Skarö County Administration directs the civil emergency response on Skarö: shelters, evacuation, and priorities for power, fuel and water between essential services. It keeps that direction until the Cabinet transfers it to national level. The Civil Contingencies Agency coordinates and supplies, but does not command, the county response.

Foreign military forces may operate on Vardland territory, in its territorial waters or in its airspace only with a Cabinet decision. Aldmoor cannot deploy forces there by its own decision, whatever its treaty obligations or its assessment of the threat. Consent may be limited in scope, place and time.

An armed attack on Vardland obliges Aldmoor to consult with Vardland on assistance. It does not oblige Aldmoor to deploy forces. Incidents below the threshold of armed attack, such as sabotage that cannot be attributed, cyber disruption or disinformation, trigger no treaty obligation. They may still justify voluntary assistance.

Only the Vardland Cabinet can officially attribute a hostile act to a state. Other Vardland actors may share evidence with the Cabinet or with Aldmoor, but cannot make an official attribution. An attribution without supporting evidence in an active fact is a political claim, not an established fact.

Repairing the Skarö subsea cable needs a cable-repair vessel on site and safe access to the fault. Repair cannot be completed in the turn in which safe access is first secured. At the earliest, it completes in the following turn. Until then, Skarö depends on backup generation and fuel deliveries by sea or air.

Military strength and readiness are qualitative in this scenario. No Argument succeeds or fails on unit counts, weapon ranges or attrition. Posture is judged from established facts and public Resources, and a claim of superiority is not evidence.

game.scenario_summary: A four-turn, six-actor total-defence crisis in a fictional northern European setting. The island county of Skarö, which belongs to the Kingdom of Vardland, lies in the Eastern Sea close to the Drevnian Federation. Skarö's only subsea power and data cable to the mainland has failed. The island now runs on backup generation, while a large Drevnian naval exercise continues nearby and conflicting stories about the cause spread online. No state of war exists. Vardland's government, armed forces, civil-contingencies agency and Skarö's county administration share responsibility for the response under overlapping rules of authority. An allied partner, the Kingdom of Aldmoor, offers help that needs Vardland's consent. Drevna seeks political advantage below the threshold of armed conflict. Each turn represents about three days. Military posture is qualitative: there are no unit counts, ranges or combat tables.

messages.text:
County Director — Defence Command can support your response within the law, at your request: transport of fuel and equipment, engineering, maritime and aerial surveillance, and protection of the military sites on Skarö (garrison, airfield, and the port/cable landing areas we share). We will not command or direct the civil response — that remains yours. We will not evacuate, restrict movement, or use force against civilians; those powers are yours.

Please tell us your priorities — fuel delivery by sea or air, backup generation support, any shelter or logistics needs, and protection of the port and cable landing site. We can have early support and surveillance available quickly, and our garrison is already at a higher internal state of readiness. We are ready to coordinate directly with your emergency staff on scene.

To our Aldmoor counterparts — we welcome your offer of assistance and have recommended to our Cabinet that it be accepted in a limited, time-scoped form. Host-nation consent is a Cabinet decision; you have our assurance that the process is moving and your proposal is being taken seriously.

Military-to-military, our current assessment: the cable failure is most likely sabotage, though not proven — a Drevnian-contracted survey vessel was recorded near the cable route hours before the failure (position and speed only). The ongoing Drevnian exercise is larger than last year's and includes landing ships; most likely signalling, but a limited seizure of Skarö cannot be ruled out and would be hard to reverse once begun. Our garrison can protect the airfield or the port/cable landing site, not both for long. We are seeking authority to reinforce — air in about one day, heavier by sea in about two.

If Cabinet consent is granted, we would value joint planning and any naval presence you could contribute near Skarö for deterrence and for safety of the cable repair. Please hold your relevant units at a state of readiness and share your own read of the exercise if you have one.

Statement from the Vardland Civil Contingencies Agency — Skarö.

The subsea cable linking Skarö to the mainland has suffered a failure. Its cause has not yet been established; an investigation is under way and no official attribution has been made. Any claim that the outage was caused by government neglect is speculation and unverified.

Skarö's backup generation is running. The County Administration is directing the response on the island and prioritising hospitals, water, heating and other essential services. Fuel resupply by sea is being arranged, and national stockpiles stand ready to support the County.

A note on roles: Skarö County Administration leads the civil response. The armed forces may support civil authorities at their request under existing rules — a support role, not a takeover. Military exercise activity in the Eastern Sea is separate from the civil response.

Please rely on official channels for information. Treat unverified claims spreading online as speculation. We will issue updates as the situation develops.

To Skarö County Administration — supply and information coordination.

Fuel: island stocks hold about five days at current use. A tanker is available at a mainland port, about one day's sailing to Skarö. We can dispatch as soon as berthing and offloading are confirmed — please confirm berth availability and unloading priorities with the port operator and county emergency direction.

Generation resilience: the national mobile-generator stockpile can cover about half of Skarö's backup generation if primary units fail. We stand ready to move these once national authority is confirmed, and we have recommended exactly that to the Cabinet today.

Medical supplies on the island are adequate for about two weeks; airlift is possible if needed. Satellite communication kits are limited — we recommend allocating them to the hospital and the County crisis centre.

Information: we have issued a factual public update today and will treat it as the common baseline. The County continues to lead the response on the island; we exist to supply and coordinate, not to command. Please direct public questions to official channels and let us know any corrections or additions you want in the next update.

Urgent supply and repair request from Skarö County Administration, which directs the civil emergency response on the island. Status: backup generation is prioritising hospitals, water and heating, but at current consumption we have about five days of backup fuel. Resupply by sea or air is now critical. We request: (1) priority dispatch of the fuel tanker now at a mainland port (about a day's sail) — we can guarantee a safe berth at Skarö's port and will coordinate offloading with the grid operator and port authorities; (2) mobile generators from the national stockpile to cover roughly half our backup load should primary units fail; (3) satellite communications kits for the county hospital and the crisis centre. Please confirm delivery schedules so we can sequence offloads against limited ferry capacity and rising outbound travel. We ask the Civil Contingencies Agency to coordinate and prioritise this resupply for Skarö under current rules. We will continue to direct the island response and keep the public informed. If prioritising fuel to Skarö formally requires a heightened-alert decision, please advise how we should prepare while the Cabinet decides. On the cable itself, we share the grid operator's assessment with you and look to Cabinet for any attribution of cause.

Support request under civil-authority arrangements. As the authority directing the civil response on Skarö, we formally request Defence Command support, within existing rules and at our request: (1) transport and logistics for fuel and generator deliveries to Skarö by sea and air; (2) engineering assistance to establish and maintain safe access at the cable landing site and at the port, which we need for the incoming fuel tanker and, later, the cable-repair vessel; (3) surveillance and protection of critical infrastructure — cable landing site, port, backup power plant, ferry terminal — and of personnel working on repair access. We ask that this support be visible where it reassures but low-profile in daily life, so the response is seen as civil-led. No evacuation or movement restrictions are requested and none are authorised under our direction. We will provide tasking priorities and keep you informed as the fuel situation develops.

Public information from Skarö County Administration. The subsea cable fault is under investigation and the response is under way. The island is running on backup generation, and hospitals, water and heating come first. Fuel resupply from the mainland has been requested and deliveries by sea are being arranged, with the port prepared to receive the tanker; mobile generators and satellite communications equipment are also being organised. Ferry capacity is limited: if you are planning to travel, expect congestion and check schedules before you leave. Please treat online claims about the cause of the outage with caution — confirmed information will be published here and on the county's official channels only. The response is civil-led, and everyone's cooperation helps keep essential services running.

Drevnian Federation — Official Statement

The Drevnian Federation categorically rejects all insinuations that it had any role in the disruption of Skarö's subsea power and data cable. No evidence supports such claims, and we call on all actors to base their assessments on facts, not speculation.

The people of Skarö deserve the swift restoration of power and connectivity. As a concrete gesture of good neighbourliness, Drevna is prepared to dispatch a civilian cable-repair vessel, with crew and equipment, to assist in repairing the fault on the earliest possible timeline, subject to normal arrangements with the competent Vardland authorities and safe access to the site.

Our naval and air exercise continues exactly as announced long in advance, conducted entirely in international waters and airspace. It poses no threat to Vardland or to anyone else. We will take every measure to avoid incidents and expect others to do the same.

We caution against the militarisation of what is, on all available evidence, a civil infrastructure problem. Reinforcing the island's garrison or deploying third-country military forces to the region would raise tensions, endanger islanders and help no one. A civilian solution, through cooperation, serves the people of Skarö best.

To the Government of the Kingdom of Aldmoor,

We address you directly and candidly. Drevna has no quarrel with Aldmoor and no interest in confrontation. The disruption of the Skarö cable is, on all available evidence, a civil infrastructure failure, and Drevna has today made a concrete civilian offer to help restore it as quickly as possible.

We would, however, be remiss not to state plainly that a decision to deploy Aldmoor military forces to Skarö would be seen as the militarisation of a civilian problem. It would place your forces in proximity to a long-announced, lawful exercise in international waters, in conditions where a single miscalculation could produce an incident serving no one. It would also deepen divisions rather than resolve them — the islanders need power and connectivity, not armoured vehicles.

We propose that this issue remain on a civilian track: Drevna's repair offer, ordinary humanitarian cooperation, and open technical communication. We are ready to enter consultations with your government and with Vardland's to agree measures that prevent misunderstanding. We sincerely hope you will weigh the consequences of any other course with care.

The Kingdom of Aldmoor stands in full solidarity with the people of Skarö and the Government of Vardland after the failure of the subsea cable. The assistance we have offered is concrete and stands — at Vardland's invitation and on Vardland's terms. We will not act on Vardland territory, in its waters or airspace without a decision by Vardland's Cabinet, and we fully respect Skarö County's leadership of the civil emergency response.

The cause of the failure has not been established. Speculation serves no one; the people of Skarö deserve facts, and we support a full and transparent investigation. We call on all states to exercise restraint and to ensure the safety of civilian shipping in the Eastern Sea, including fuel resupply and any cable--repair operations.

Aldmoor notes the Drevnian exercise in international waters south-east of Skarö. Exercises in international waters are a lawful right, and we respect that fully.

At the same time, Skarö depends on civilian fuel resupply and cable repair in the near term. We expect those operations to proceed safely and without interference, and we will maintain a presence in the area accordingly.

We note your stated humanitarian concern for the people of Skarö. The most useful contribution any state can make now is restraint and factual communication. Our channels with your government remain open.

Statement from the Prime Minister's office. The Government's first priority is the safety, warmth and wellbeing of the people of Skarö. Backup generation is holding; fuel and generators are being moved to the island, and we are working to bring a cable-repair vessel to the fault as soon as safe access is possible. The cause of the failure has not been established. We have opened an independent, transparent technical investigation and will publish its findings. The emergency response on the island remains directed by Skarö County Administration, with the full backing of national authorities. All offers of assistance will be judged only by the needs of Skarö's people and on terms Vardland itself controls; we are managing this emergency with our own national resources and do not require foreign humanitarian assistance. We are monitoring all activity in the Eastern Sea and expect every state to respect international law and refrain from any interference with civilian repair and supply operations vital to Skarö.

We warmly welcome Aldmoor's offer of support and wish to take it up on clear terms that Vardland controls, as our alliance presumes. We request: (1) Aldmoor maritime surveillance patrols in the international waters adjacent to Skarö, with limited, time-boxed overflight of Vardland airspace to be authorised by our Cabinet decision; (2) engineering or cable-repair assistance, including any vessel or dive assets Aldmoor can spare, to restore the Skarö cable; and (3) contingency logistics and fuel support if the outage extends beyond two weeks. We are not requesting ground forces on Skarö at this time. Our Cabinet will formalise consent with a defined scope, place and time. Please confirm availability and any capabilities you can offer, so we can move quickly.

The Vardland Government thanks the Drevnian Federation for its offer of humanitarian and technical assistance to the people of Skarö. The response to this infrastructure failure is being fully managed by Vardland's national authorities and Skarö County Administration, using our own resources, and we therefore do not require foreign assistance at this time. We are confident the Drevnian Federation will ensure that its ongoing exercise remains in international waters and takes every precaution not to interfere with civilian repair and supply operations that are critical to Skarö's population. We remain open to normal, professional contact between our authorities.

Civil Contingencies Agency to Skarö County Administration. Confirming our coordination role under current rules and acting on your request. Resupply: the fuel tanker at the mainland port is available and we are treating its dispatch to Skarö as the top national priority — roughly one day's sailing once you confirm the berth; we will sequence offloading against your ferry capacity and advise delivery slots. Mobile generators: we will release units from the national stockpile covering about half your backup load should primary units fail, matched to the same sea leg where possible. Satellite communication kits: limited stockpile is reserved for the county hospital and the crisis centre, plus standby for the water plant if supply allows. On formal authority: under current rules we can coordinate and advise, but directing fuel, generators and medical supplies across counties formally requires a Cabinet decision. We are pressing for heightened alert or a targeted delegation now, before fuel runs low, and will advise you immediately once decided. We fully align with your public line — cause not established, response civil-led, County in charge on the island. We recommend a joint next public update on your channels covering confirmed delivery schedules and generator status, to hold the factual baseline against rumour. Please confirm the berth and offloading slots so we can fix the schedule.

Civil Contingencies Agency — urgent recommendation for a decision on cross-county supply authority. Skarö has about five days of backup fuel; resupply is the binding constraint. The tanker at a mainland port is available, about a day's sail if it is granted priority; mobile generators (about half of Skarö's backup load) and satellite kits for the hospital and crisis centre are available from national stockpiles. Under current rules the Agency can coordinate, but formally directing fuel, generators and medical supplies across counties requires Cabinet authority. We recommend heightened alert, or at minimum a targeted delegation, granted now — well ahead of the next resupply cycle, not in extremis. For Cabinet's planning: the contracted cable-repair vessel is in dry dock and cannot sail for several days, so repair cannot complete before next turn at the earliest; this should frame public expectations of restoration timelines. Evidence for Cabinet's use: we have traced part of the online rumour campaign to accounts outside Vardland, moderate confidence; the full package is available to you — we offer evidence, attribution rests with Cabinet. We also note the standing offers of civilian repair assistance; acceptance, decline and their security terms are Cabinet's call. We propose agreeing one coordinated public line; the Agency stands ready to brief at any time.

Civil Contingencies Agency — coordination of military support to the civil Skarö response. As support-to-civil under current rules, we ask Defence Command to be ready to assist Skarö's civil authorities, at the County's request, with transport and engineering for fuel and generator movement, surveillance of the sea-approach route, and protection of military sites; and to designate a single liaison for logistics and supply-route coordination. Parameters remain: the response is civil-led, the County directs on the island, and Defence does not order evacuation, restrict civilian movement or use force against civilians — those powers sit with civil authorities. If the Cabinet adjusts alert posture, we will re-coordinate immediately. We also ask that public messaging keep military support clearly distinct from the civil response to preserve public trust. Please confirm the liaison point and we will route requests through it.

Prime Minister's Office to the Kingdom of Aldmoor. On the strength of your government's standing offer and after full consultation, the Vardland Cabinet has formally decided, under our host-nation consent procedures, to accept your assistance on limited, time-boxed terms: (1) surveillance and overflight by Aldmoor aircraft over defined areas of the Eastern Sea covering the Skarö cable route and the fuel resupply corridor, for early warning and the safety of civilian shipping during the repair and resupply operation; (2) technical and logistics support to the cable-repair and fuel-resupply effort, coordinated through the Civil Contingencies Agency and Defence Command. Scope limits: no Aldmoor ground forces on Skarö; no operations beyond the defined sea/air areas; consent runs until the cable is restored or 30 days, whichever is earlier, and is renewable by Cabinet decision; Vardland retains full authority over the response and may adjust terms at any time on notice.

Please confirm acceptance, designate points of contact for our Defence Command and Civil Contingencies Agency, and advise when surveillance capabilities can be brought to bear. We intend to announce the broad outlines of this arrangement publicly, on the same terms we have agreed here, so that the basis and limits are transparent to all.

Cabinet decision — Skarö resupply and repair. We approve and give highest national priority to the County Administration's urgent request: (1) the fuel tanker now at the mainland port is to sail without delay for Skarö (approximately one day's sail), with the county's guaranteed berth and offloading plan as coordinated; (2) mobile generators from the national stockpile to cover roughly half the backup load, should primary units fail; (3) satellite communications kits for the county hospital and the crisis centre. The Civil Contingencies Agency is directed to coordinate and sequence these deliveries with the county, the grid operator and the port, and to confirm delivery schedules to the county at the earliest opportunity so that offloads can be sequenced against limited ferry capacity. The county continues to direct the island emergency response; the Cabinet takes no ordering role in the county's operations. No heightened-alert declaration is required for these measures under current law; we will keep alert options under active review and act if resupply, repair access or the security picture deteriorates. Any Treasury implications of extended support beyond two weeks will be handled by an extraordinary budget decision rather than by slowing deliveries.

Statement from the Government of Vardland — Skarö.

The Government's first priority is the safety and supply of the people of Skarö. The subsea cable failure is under a full, transparent investigation; no attribution of cause has been made, and we will publish what is established as it becomes reliable. Any claim that the outage stems from government neglect, or that a specific state caused it, is speculation until evidence establishes it.

The response is civil-led: Skarö County Administration directs the island response, and the full weight of the state stands behind it. We confirm that urgent resupply is under way — a fuel tanker is sailing without delay, and mobile generators and satellite communications equipment are on their way to the island.

To protect this civilian effort and the safety of all shipping while a large exercise continues nearby, the Cabinet has consented to limited, time-boxed assistance from our ally Aldmoor: surveillance and overflight for early warning, and technical support to the repair — on terms Vardland controls and sets. There will be no foreign ground forces on Skarö. This is measured, lawful and transparent support for a civilian emergency, not escalation.

We respect the exercise rights of all states in international waters and expect them to respect the safety of the civilian ships repairing our cable and resupplying the island. We call on all parties to exercise restraint and to let facts, not speculation, guide the discussion. Reliable information will be published through official channels.

Defence Command to Skarö County Administration. We formally accept your support request under the existing civil-authority arrangements and will act at your direction and within the law. Concretely we will provide and maintain: (1) transport and logistics for fuel and generator movements to Skarö by sea and air, including monitoring of the approaches used by the incoming fuel tanker; (2) engineering assistance to establish and keep safe access at the cable landing site and at the port; (3) surveillance and protection of the cable landing site, port, backup power plant and ferry terminal, and of personnel working on repair access. Our presence will be visible where it reassures and low-profile in daily life, with the response clearly civil-led. We will not introduce evacuation orders or movement restrictions; those remain yours and are not authorised under our support. Please send your tasking priorities and the tanker programme as soon as possible so we can coordinate schedules and the safety of the repair site. We will continue to treat the investigation and the exercise separately, as you have advised.

Defence Command — assessment and recommendation. (1) We have accepted Skarö County's formal request for military support to the civil response (transport, engineering, surveillance, protection of critical infrastructure) and are delivering it within existing rules. This does not, however, authorise reinforcing the Skarö garrison. (2) The garrison is small and can currently protect either the airfield or the port and cable-landing complex, not both for long. Prompt declaration of heightened alert would authorise moving additional units onto Skarö — first elements by air in about one day, heavier units by sea in about two — plus reservist call-up and CCA cross-county powers over fuel and generators. We recommend declaring it now, presented as prudent protection of infrastructure and islanders, so it is read as preparedness rather than reaction. (3) We recommend early, time-boxed consideration of limited Aldmoor support under host-nation consent should the situation deteriorate; we will not invite any presence absent a Cabinet decision, and any consent could be scoped narrowly. (4) On cause: our naval surveillance recorded the Drevnian-contracted survey vessel moving slowly along the cable route about twelve hours before the failure. The recording shows position and speed only, not activity. We make no attribution — that is for the Cabinet — but recommend the technical investigation prioritise that vessel's records. We stand ready to brief at any time.

Vardland Defence Command — operational update. At the formal request of Skarö County Administration, and within the existing rules for military support to civil authorities, the armed forces are assisting the civil-led response on Skarö with transport and logistics for fuel and generators, engineering support for safe access at the cable landing site and port, and surveillance and protection of critical infrastructure and of personnel working to restore service. The emergency response on the island remains directed by the County Administration; our role is support, not command. We will not order evacuations or restrict movement — those are civil powers and remain with civil authorities. Monitoring of the Eastern Sea continues, and every party must respect international law and the safety of civilian shipping supplying Skarö. The response is civil-led, and any claim that the armed forces are taking over the emergency is false.

Statement from the Drevnian Federation on the situation in the Eastern Sea.

The failure of the Skarö power and data cable is a serious matter for the people of the island. Drevna's position is clear: we had no hand in this failure, and we have consistently urged calm and factual communication. We support a full, transparent, evidence-based investigation so that the cause is established without speculation.

We welcome the assurance that the emergency response on Skarö is civil-led and being managed by the county and by Vardland's national authorities. Drevna agrees that this is a civil infrastructure matter, and that no foreign military deployment on Skarö is needed or appropriate. The people of Skarö need fuel, generators and a working cable - not soldiers.

Our offer to send a Drevnian civilian cable-repair vessel, made purely as a gesture of good neighbourliness and subject entirely to Vardland's wishes, remains on the table. We fully respect Vardland's sovereign decision to manage the response with its own national resources, and we will not press the matter. Should Vardland ask, the vessel can be activated at short notice, with no conditions.

The Drevnian exercise continues in international waters, in full compliance with international law. We have given strict instructions to keep all exercise manoeuvres well clear of civilian shipping, including the fuel route to Skarö and any cable-repair operation. We expect all states to show the same restraint and to refrain from speculation and from any action that could endanger civilian supply and repair.

We urge everyone to rely on official information and to treat unverified claims, in whatever direction, as speculation. Drevna will act responsibly.

Private - from the Drevnian Federation to the Government of Vardland.

We have received the Government's reply to our offer of assistance and we respect it fully. Managing this emergency with national resources is Vardland's sovereign decision, and we will not second-guess it. Our civilian cable-repair vessel offer stands and can be activated at short notice whenever Vardland judges it useful - no conditions, no strings attached.

To be plain about our intentions: our exercise will remain in international waters, and we are ready to agree practical measures to keep all manoeuvres well clear of the fuel route to Skarö and of any cable-repair operation. We propose a working-level channel to deconflict civilian maritime traffic so that misunderstandings are avoided. We ask for nothing in return.

We also wish to state, plainly and privately: in our assessment, this is a civil infrastructure matter and should be handled as one. The introduction of third-country military forces into the Eastern Sea in connection with a cable fault would be disproportionate, would raise the temperature, and would not help a single household on Skarö. We trust Vardland's government to act in the best interests of its own people.

Our channels remain open for professional contact at any level. We hope the investigation proceeds quickly and transparently, and if it raises questions for Drevna through official channels, we will respond properly and in good faith.

Private - from the Drevnian Federation to the Kingdom of Aldmoor.

Thank you for your message. We are in full agreement that civilian fuel resupply and cable repair must proceed safely and without interference, and we give you our assurance on that point. The Drevnian exercise is conducted in international waters in full compliance with international law, and our commanders have strict orders to keep all manoeuvres well clear of the shipping routes serving Skarö and of any cable-repair operation.

If Aldmoor wishes, we are ready to establish a practical working-level channel for maritime deconfliction so that both our forces and civilian traffic in the Eastern Sea are kept safe. The best way to ensure no incident is to prevent misunderstandings before they arise.

We note and welcome your commitment to act only at Vardland's invitation and on Vardland's terms, and we note that Vardland has stated it is managing this response with its own national resources. We agree with that approach. In our assessment, a cable fault is a civil infrastructure matter; additional foreign military forces in the area would raise the temperature without helping the people of Skarö and would create risks no one needs. Drevna's civilian repair-vessel offer to Vardland stands and is purely humanitarian.

Our channels remain open, and we hope the people of Skarö get the facts, the fuel and the repaired cable they need without further drama. Restraint on all sides serves everyone.

Defence Command — Skarö County confirms and specifies its support requests. Priorities: (1) transport of fuel by sea and any airlift of generators or satellite-communication kits; (2) engineering support to secure and prepare the cable landing site and the port for repair access and safe supply; (3) maritime and aerial surveillance of the approaches to Skarö, the port and the cable landing site; (4) protection of the military sites we share (garrison, airfield, port/cable landing areas).

Our requirement on profile: we need this support effective in capability yet low in visibility — the public face of this response must remain civil. We will publish that armed forces are assisting at the County's request in a supporting role, not taking over. No evacuation, movement restrictions or force against civilians: those powers remain with civil authorities.

Please confirm early availability and one on-scene liaison point to coordinate with our emergency staff, and advise of any maritime traffic around Skarö relevant to the fuel tanker's passage.

CCA — Skarö County confirms the essentials from your side.

Berth and offloading: the port berth and fuel offloading are county priorities. I am directing the port operator to have the berth, offloading and storage ready, with hospitals, water, heating and other essential services first in the allocation. Please dispatch the tanker as soon as possible and confirm ETA and cargo details.

Generation: agreed on mobile generators — they could cover about half our backup load if primary units fail. We will have connection sites and staff ready; please move them as soon as national authority is confirmed and confirm delivery schedule and whether airlift is planned for any of it. Satellite-communication kits: hospital and County crisis centre confirmed.

For the next update, please include practical ferry and travel information for residents, and a clear sentence that Skarö County Administration continues to lead the civil response, with national authorities and the armed forces in a supporting role at the County's request. Repeating that point counters the 'military takeover' narrative circulating online.

Message from Skarö County Administration to the people of Skarö.

Your safety, warmth and essential services come first. Backup generation is running; hospitals, water and heating remain prioritised. A fuel tanker is standing by to sail, and we have confirmed berth and offloading priority at the port. Additional generators are being prepared on the mainland to reinforce us if needed.

The cause of the cable fault has not been established. Claims circulating online — about who caused it, or that someone is taking over our response — are speculation. The facts: Skarö County Administration leads this emergency response, and national authorities, including the armed forces in a strictly supporting role at our request, help us. Nothing is being taken over.

We know some of you are considering leaving by ferry. That is your choice; we ask nothing more than calm and preparation. Ferry and travel information will be published on official channels as it is confirmed.

Use official sources. If you need help, contact our crisis centre. We will keep you informed, with facts, as the situation develops.

Your Excellencies — thank you for your trust and for the clear terms. The Kingdom of Aldmoor accepts your request and confirms as follows:

1) Maritime surveillance patrols in the international waters adjacent to Skarö can begin within approximately one day of your Cabinet's formal decision, with limited, time-boxed overflight of Vardland airspace exactly as and when the Cabinet authorises it.
2) Engineering and cable-repair assistance: an Aldmoor-operated cable-repair vessel can be on station within two days of a request, with dive and survey assets in support as needed. We will operate within Vardland's repair scheme and the County's priorities.
3) Contingency logistics and fuel support: standing offer should the outage extend beyond two weeks.

We understand the role as limited, defined and time-bound — no ground forces on Skarö at this time — with scope, place and time set by the Cabinet and every element ending by mutual agreement on a defined end point. Nothing will be activated before your decision. Vardland retains full control of all activity on its territory, waters and airspace.

Separately and privately: we are prepared to share a sanitised technical brief on the survey vessel observed near the cable route in the hours before the failure, in a form that protects our sources and methods. Sanitised material carries lower evidential weight than our full analysis, but it may assist your investigation. Attribution remains entirely the Vardland Cabinet's decision; we will make no public claim.

We stand ready for joint planning with your Defence Command at your convenience.

Noted and agreed. We are holding our relevant units at readiness and are ready for joint planning immediately.

Our read of the Drevnian exercise, for your assessment: the scale and composition — notably landing ships — exceed last year's, and the disposition appears carefully designed to stay below any threshold that would engage the mutual-defence treaty. We assess the most likely purpose as coercive signalling aimed at shaping the response to the cable failure and deterring reinforcement of Skarö. We do not judge a seizure to be the base case, but a limited seizure cannot be excluded and would be hard to reverse once begun — your assessment aligns with ours.

We therefore recommend: joint planning now; a visible Aldmoor naval presence near Skarö in international waters as a deterrent and for the safety of the cable repair; continued close monitoring. We are ready to contribute escort and naval presence for fuel and supply shipments and for the repair operation.

On the survey vessel: we can provide a sanitised intelligence summary of what we hold, through agreed channels, protecting our collection methods. It is not an official attribution — that decision rests with your Cabinet.

Our two-day cable-repair vessel response stands. We suggest we agree a common operational picture before repair assets deploy, so that safe access is confirmed under your authorities' decision and the repair can proceed without delay.

Thank you for your letter; we have read it with care.

Aldmoor's position is straightforward. We act only in support of Vardland, at Vardland's request and within the decisions Vardland alone makes over its territory, waters and airspace. Our assistance is limited, time-bound and conducted strictly under international law. We have no quarrel with the Drevnian Federation, no interest in confrontation, and no intention of militarising a civilian problem.

Equally plainly: restoring power and connectivity to Skarö is an urgent civilian need. Every state has an interest in letting repair and resupply operations proceed safely and without interference. We note your assurance that your exercise is conducted so as to avoid incidents, and we expect that commitment to hold in practice, including with respect to civilian repair and supply traffic.

We remain open to technical and safety-of-navigation communication on that basis. The situation will be defined by events and by responsible conduct, not by labels.

Defence Command — for the Cabinet's decision on alert posture.

Assessment (shared with Aldmoor, consistent with our restricted assessment): the Drevnian exercise is larger than last year's and includes landing ships; its disposition appears carefully kept below any threshold that would engage the treaty. Most likely it is coercive signalling to shape the response to the cable failure and to deter reinforcement. A limited seizure cannot be ruled out and would be hard to reverse once begun.

Recommendation: declare heightened alert now — partial and Skarö-focused at minimum. It gives Defence Command lawful authority to airlift a first response (about one day) and move heavier units by sea (about two days), and it gives the Civil Contingencies Agency cross-county powers over fuel, generators and medical supplies. Each day of delay lengthens the exposure of the airfield, port and cable-landing site, which the small garrison cannot protect simultaneously for long.

On foreign assistance: we welcome the limited, time-boxed Aldmoor consent already granted (surveillance/overflight and technical repair support; no foreign ground forces). An Aldmoor presence in international waters needs no consent and, with your assent, supports safe supply and repair; any role in Vardland territorial waters or airspace beyond the current scope should be decided deliberately and scoped in place and time.

On the Drevnian repair-vessel offer: we recommend it be handled strictly on safety, access and Vardland's control of the operation, not as evidence about cause. Drevna must not set the pace or presence near the cable site.

We stand ready to brief you in detail and to execute immediately onyour decision.

Defence Command confirms, in response to the County's request and CCA coordination.

Liaison: a single on-scene liaison point is stood up effective now — Defence Liaison Skarö — reachable through the County emergency staff and the CCA coordination cell, with authority to task our support within current law.

Early availability, as tasked by the County and limited to support roles: (1) transport of fuel by sea and airlift for generators and satellite-communication kits; (2) engineering support to secure and prepare the cable landing site and port; (3) maritime and aerial surveillance of the approaches, the port and the cable landing site; (4) protection of the shared military sites (garrison, airfield, port/cable-landing areas). These tasks fall within support-to-civil and require no alert declaration.

Traffic advisory: we are maintaining maritime surveillance of the approaches and will give the County timely advisories relevant to the tanker's passage, as requested. The Drevnian exercise command has publicly committed to staying clear of civilian shipping; we will monitor and report any deviation.

Profile: agreed. Support remains at the County's request, low in visibility, civil-led in public face. We confirm no evacuation, movement restrictions or force against civilians — those powers sit with civil authorities. Our public messaging will continue to describe a strictlysupporting role.

Joint planning agreed. Confirmations on our side.

Assessment: our restricted assessment aligns with yours — the exercise is larger than last year's, includes landing ships, and its disposition appears disciplined below the mutual-defence threshold. Most likely coercive signalling to shape the response to the cable failure and deter reinforcement; a limited seizure cannot be excluded and would be hard to reverse. We are using this in our recommendation to the Cabinet on alert posture.

Consent status: the Cabinet has granted limited, time-boxed consent for your surveillance and overflight and technical support to the repair, on terms Vardland controls; no foreign ground forces on Skarö. A visible naval presence in international waters needs no host-nation consent and, in our view, usefully supports safe supply and repair; any presence in Vardland territorial waters or airspace beyond the current scope must be decided by the Cabinet — we will support a scoped request.

Intelligence: we accept your sanitised summary on the survey vessel through agreed channels. It will inform our government's investigation and will not be presented as official attribution, which rests with our Cabinet.

Repair: the decision that access is safe rests with our civil authorities in coordination with the Cabinet. We will maintain the common operational picture with you so your repair vessel can deploy without delay once access is confirmed.

We will advise you immediately on any change inalert posture.

CCA to Skarö County — resupply confirmation and sequencing.

1) Fuel: under Cabinet direction the tanker sails without delay; ETA approximately one day, subject to safe passage. Berth and offloading priority as the County directs — we will confirm cargo details and ETA to the port operator today so offloading can be sequenced against limited ferry capacity.

2) Generators: release from the national stockpile is authorised. We will sequence them sea-first against ferry capacity, with airlift reserved for priority items — the satellite-communication kits for the hospital and county crisis centre move by air as a priority. Please reconfirm which connection sites to prioritise for the delivered units and any port load limits for coordination.

3) Public information: we will surge national supply/logistics updates, including for radio on the island given reduced internet, and will hold the line that Skarö County leads the response with national support. Please publish practical ferry and travel information through County and official channels as confirmed; we will point residents to them. We propose a joint update within the next 24 hours once schedules are fixed. Anything you need from us for that, say the word.

CCA to Cabinet — authority, repair timeline and information coordination.

1) Cross-county supply authority: recommend securing it now, not in extremis. Fuel on Skarö is about five days at current use; each tanker is about a day's sail; the contracted cable-repair vessel remains in dry dock for several days, so the cable cannot be restored this turn and resupply must be sustained and repeatable across counties. A targeted delegation, or a partial heightened alert limited to supply functions, would let us direct fuel, generators and medical supplies across county lines without friction if competing county demands arise. We can run the current sequence without it, but the authority should exist before day three.

2) Disinformation: our tracing — moderate confidence, evidence, not attribution — shows part of the rumour surge is amplified from foreign accounts, and the open-source monitor shows Drevnian state media pushing an 'Aldmoor base' narrative. We recommend one coordinated public-information plan: radio-forward for the island, quick rebuttals of the four circulating narratives, and messaging that leads with 'County directs, Defence supports at County request', since any visible military footprint will be framed as takeover.

3) Drevna repair offer: recommend holding for now. Aldmoor technical support plus our own contracted vessel once it sails cover the repair path; accepting Drevna's vessel this early concedes agenda-setting and complicates investigation optics. Reassess only if the repair timeline slips.

4) We will hold the exact Cabinet/County public line (civil-led, cause unestablished, speculation labelled as such). Request confirmation of the joint update plan and a decision on supply authority.

Vardland Civil Contingencies Agency — Skarö supply update.

The Civil Contingencies Agency is coordinating the national resupply behind Skarö County Administration, which continues to direct the on-island response. Confirmed: the fuel tanker for Skarö is under way, approximately one day's sailing, with berth priority for essential services — hospitals, water and heating — as directed by the County. Mobile generators from the national stockpile are being prepared and will be delivered against ferry capacity, with priority equipment, including satellite communications for the hospital and the county crisis centre, moving by air. Medical supplies remain adequate, with arrangements standing by.

The cause of the cable fault has not been established. Claims that the government neglected the cable, that a foreign takeover is under way, or that a specific state caused the failure are speculation until evidence establishes otherwise. Armed forces personnel on Skarö act in a strictly supporting role at the County's request; the response is civil-led.

On Skarö, where internet capacity is reduced, official information continues via radio and County channels. Practical ferry and travel information will be published through County and official channels as confirmed.

We will publish reliable facts as they are established. Please rely on official sources.

Skarö County Administration to CCA. Berth and offloading confirmed. The county grants the incoming fuel tanker priority berth at Skarö port, and we will hold offloading slots for it sequentially, sequenced against ferry sailings as you advise. Fuel allocation on the island is prioritised for hospitals, water, heating and essential services; we will confirm the detailed storage and distribution plan once cargo details are firm.

We accept the mobile generator package (covering about half the backup load should primary units fail) and the satellite communication kits for the county hospital and the crisis centre, with standby for the water plant if supply allows, matched to the same sea leg. Please confirm the tanker's sail and estimated time of arrival, the offloading schedule, and generator movement timing at the earliest opportunity so we can publish confirmed schedules and hand the programme to Defence Command for route monitoring. Skarö County Administration to Defence Command. Support request confirmed and accepted by you; thank you. Our tasking priorities, to be refined as schedules firm:

(1) Transport and logistics for the fuel tanker and generator sea leg, including monitoring of the approaches used by the incoming tanker; (2) engineering assistance to establish and keep safe access at the cable landing site and at the port; (3) low-profile surveillance and protection of the cable landing site, port, backup power plant and ferry terminal, and of personnel working on repair access.

We will send the tanker programme and berth slots as soon as CCA confirms sail and ETA. Once confirmed, we ask you to coordinate route monitoring accordingly. Please designate one on-scene liaison point for the county crisis centre and give us a first read on the surveillance picture around Skarö.

We confirm the arrangement as you stated and as we published: presence visible where it reassures, low-profile in daily life, response clearly civil-led. No evacuation orders or movement restrictions are being introduced.

Update from Skarö County Administration to residents.

Your safety and supply are our first priority, and help is on the way. A fuel tanker is sailing to Skarö and is expected within about a day; mobile generators and satellite communication equipment are being delivered for the hospital and the crisis centre. The County Administration directs the island's emergency response. Our armed forces assist in transport, engineering and protection only — this is a civilian emergency, led by the county, and no one is taking over.

The cause of the cable failure has not yet been established. The investigation is transparent and we will report what is confirmed as it becomes reliable. Until then, please treat claims about who is responsible — and any suggestion of a military takeover — as speculation and rely on official channels.

We will publish confirmed delivery schedules, generator status and travel information for the ferries as soon as they are fixed. Hospitals, water, heating and essential services remain prioritised. Stay calm, help your neighbours, and check official county channels for the next update.

Minister, we have read your letter with equal care. Let us be plain in reply.

We share your view that this is a civilian emergency and that nothing about it should become a military confrontation. For that reason we welcome your own description of the assistance Aldmoor is providing and we trust it will remain strictly as Vardland has announced: limited in scope, time-bound, conducted under international law and under Vardland's control, with no ground forces and no permanent presence anywhere on or near Skarö.

For our part we repeat what we have said publicly: the Drevnian Federation had no part in the cable failure, and our long-announced autumn exercise will continue fully within international waters and airspace, well clear of civilian shipping and of any repair and resupply operations serving Skarö. We accept your proposal for technical and safety-of-navigation communication and are ready to establish a working-level channel immediately, so that neither side is ever surprised by movement in the Eastern Sea.

Statement of the Drevnian Federation on the situation around Skarö.

The cause of the failure of the Skarö subsea cable has not been established, and the Drevnian Federation had no part in it. We said so from the first hour and we will say so as often as needed. The people of Skarö deserve facts and warmth, not suspicion and not escalation.

Vardland's own Government confirms that its response is civil-led, that its armed forces act only in support of civilian authorities at the County's request, and that no foreign ground forces will be deployed to Skarö. We welcome that confirmation. This is a civilian emergency and it should be resolved by civilian means. The shortest road to restoring power and connectivity is to repair the cable — a task for civilian cable operators, not for military forces.

Our long-announced autumn exercise continues in international waters and airspace, conducted strictly in accordance with international law and well clear of civilian shipping routes serving Skarö, the cable landing site and any repair operation. We have given safety assurances and we will honour them. We have also accepted a practical channel for technical and safety-of-navigation communication, so that civilian traffic is never endangered by anyone's movements.

We take note of the description of foreign military assistance to Vardland as limited and time-bound. We trust that is precisely what it will remain, and that no permanent foreign military presence or bases will appear in this region under cover of an emergency. Escalation serves no one. What the islanders need is power, heat and connectivity — not military posturing around their homes.

Drevna remains ready to help in a civilian capacity. Our cable-repair vessel offer stands, at no cost and with no conditions beyond the consent of Vardland's authorities.

Your Excellency,

We take your Government's description of any external assistance as limited and time-bound. We trust it will remain exactly that: every state in the region benefits from restraint at a time like this.

From the Government of the Kingdom of Aldmoor to the Prime Minister's Office of Vardland.

The Kingdom of Aldmoor formally accepts the assistance package set out in the Cabinet's decision of today, which matches the limited, clearly defined assistance we offered.
